jobs.description:
VIDIZMO is an AI software company headquartered in Tysons, Virginia. We build Nexus, AI Intelligence Hub, AI Live Insight and Redactor, a product family that lets an organization search, analyze, redact and act on its unstructured data, where video, audio, images, documents and text are treated as equal first-class sources rather than one format with the rest bolted on. More than 100 customers run VIDIZMO in production across public safety and justice, government, healthcare, financial services, education, legal, manufacturing and energy, and much of that installed base runs on premises, in air-gapped environments, or in FedRAMP High environments through our hosting partners, on a CJIS Security Policy-aligned architecture.

We are an independent software vendor. We build and support the software, and the channel sells it, with qualified partners also installing, delivering and supporting deployments for their own clients. That model shapes almost every role here: the people we hire spend their time making partners and customers successful rather than pushing paper through a direct sales funnel.

As we continue to expand our footprint across public sector and enterprise markets, we are building a world-class channel organization to accelerate growth through strategic partners, resellers, and system integrators.

Role Summary

We are seeking an experienced Channel AM to design, build, and scale our partner-driven sales engine. This role is responsible for recruiting and managing a network of resellers, system integrators, and technology partners, and for driving measurable revenue growth through those relationships — with a particular focus on public sector and public safety markets.

The ideal candidate has a proven, quantifiable track record in IT/enterprise software sales — SaaS experience strongly preferred — and understands how to navigate long government sales cycles, procurement processes, and partner-led go-to-market strategies.

Key Responsibilities

Partner Recruitment & Onboarding

  • Identify, evaluate, and recruit new channel partners including resellers, system integrators (SIs), and technology alliance partners
  • Design and execute structured onboarding programs to enable partners to sell VIDIZMO's platform effectively
  • Build a scalable partner tiering and certification framework

Revenue Growth & Pipeline Management

  • Own and drive channel-sourced revenue targets on a quarterly and annual basis
  • Build joint pipeline with partners and actively manage deal registration, forecasting, and progression
  • Support partners through complex, multi-stakeholder public sector sales cycles

Go-to-Market Strategy

  • Develop joint go-to-market plans, campaigns, and enablement content with key partners
  • Collaborate with marketing to build co-branded materials, case studies, and public sector-specific positioning (e.g., public safety, law enforcement, justice, transportation)
  • Identify white-space opportunities within existing partner accounts

Partner Management & Enablement

  • Conduct regular business reviews (QBRs) with partners to track performance against targets
  • Provide technical and sales enablement training to ensure partners can articulate VIDIZMO's value proposition confidently
  • Act as the primary escalation point for partner-related issues, ensuring high satisfaction and retention

Commercial & Contractual Ownership

  • Negotiate partner agreements, margin structures, and deal registration terms
  • Ensure compliance with internal pricing, discounting, and legal guidelines
  • Maintain accurate records of partner agreements, performance data, and pipeline in CRM

Cross-Functional Collaboration

  • Work closely with direct sales, product, and customer success teams to ensure a seamless partner-assisted sales motion
  • Provide market feedback to product and leadership on public sector and public safety buyer needs

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Business, Marketing, IT, or a related field (MBA preferred)
  • 5+ years of experience in IT/enterprise software sales, channel sales, or partnership management
  • Demonstrated, quantifiable track record of quota attainment (e.g., % of quota achieved, average deal size, peer ranking within sales team)
  • Prior experience selling into the public sector required; experience in public safety (law enforcement, emergency management, justice/courts, homeland security) strongly preferred
  • Experience selling SaaS or cloud-based enterprise software strongly preferred
  • Proven experience building and scaling a channel/partner ecosystem from the ground up or significantly growing an existing one
  • Strong understanding of government procurement processes, RFPs, and public sector buying cycles
  • Excellent negotiation, relationship-building, and stakeholder management skills
  • Proficiency with CRM tools (Salesforce, HubSpot, or similar) for pipeline and partner management

Preferred Qualifications

  • Existing relationships with resellers or system integrators serving public safety or government agencies
  • Experience with AI, video intelligence, data analytics, or related enterprise software categories
  • Familiarity with FedRAMP, StateRAMP, or other public sector compliance/procurement frameworks
  • Experience managing partner programs across multiple U.S. states or international markets

What We Offer

  • Competitive base salary with uncapped, performance-based commission structure
  • Opportunity to build and shape a channel program from an early stage
  • Work with a Microsoft Solutions Partner at the forefront of AI innovation
  • High-ownership culture with direct access to leadership
  • Exposure to cutting-edge AI/LLM-powered enterprise products

VIDIZMO is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

jobs.description:
Director Engineering & Project Delivery

Location: Remote, with travel to headquarters in Ormond Beach, FL, and customer sites
Reports To: Chief Strategy & Services Officer
Employment Type: Full-time
Travel: Up to 40%, domestic and international
Schedule: Five days per week; occasional extended hours, weekends, and off-hours customer support required

Position Summary

We are seeking an experienced Director of GMP Engineering & Project Delivery to build and lead an integrated delivery function supporting customers in regulated pharmaceutical, biotechnology, medical device, and life sciences environments.

This leader will establish the strategy, standards, staffing model, and commercial approach that connect design, procurement, fabrication, installation, qualification, validation, and turnover into a coordinated offering. The role partners closely with established Commissioning, Qualification & Validation (CQV), Field Service, and Certification teams while those groups retain responsibility for their respective operations.

The ideal candidate combines deep technical expertise in GMP facilities, equipment, and computerized systems with experience building technical organizations, managing third-party engineering partners, and delivering projects against quality, schedule, and financial commitments.

Key Responsibilities

Delivery Strategy & Team Development

  • Build the GMP delivery function, including service offerings, operating structure, staffing plans, billing rates, utilization targets, and phased hiring criteria.
  • Establish a repeatable delivery approach that connects engineering, manufacturing, installation, qualification, and turnover.
  • Align standards, resources, and customer commitments across CQV, Field Service, Certification, and other internal teams.
  • Determine which capabilities to maintain internally and which to support through qualified partners.
  • Partner with functional leaders to recruit, develop, and mentor multidisciplinary technical talent.
  • Create competency frameworks and career development paths to support long-term team growth.

Engineering, Qualification & Validation

  • Serve as the technical authority for GMP facility and equipment design, including user requirements, basis of design, design rationale, and formal design reviews.
  • Establish engineering and validation standards, document templates, and review procedures.
  • Develop risk-based approaches to computer system validation (CSV) and computer software assurance (CSA) in coordination with CQV.
  • Provide oversight of data integrity, electronic records and signatures, audit trails, and validated computerized systems.
  • Resolve complex technical issues involving cleanroom classification, containment, air handling, utilities, material and personnel flow, and contamination control.
  • Support the expansion of certification services, including biological safety cabinets, HEPA filtration, cleanroom classification, vaporized hydrogen peroxide biodecontamination, and requalification.
  • Ensure work meets applicable cGMP requirements and relevant standards, including FDA regulations, EU GMP Annexes 1 and 11, ISO 14644, NSF/ANSI 49, GAMP 5, and ISPE guidance.

Vendor & Project Oversight

  • Select, qualify, and technically manage vendors supporting automation, controls, and process engineering.
  • Define vendor scope, evaluate proposals, review technical specifications, and approve deliverables.
  • Review vendor designs, software and control specifications, protocols, and turnover packages for alignment with project qualification requirements.
  • Maintain approved vendor and supplier qualification programs in partnership with Quality.
  • Establish project controls for schedules, costs, earned value, risks, and change management.
  • Manage change orders for internally delivered work, including scope identification, pricing, and customer discussions.
  • Coordinate procurement, expediting, installation supervision, and transition to qualification with existing corporate functions.

Financial & Customer Leadership

  • Own financial performance for the function, including revenue, billable utilization, realized billing rates, gross margin, and EBITDA contribution.
  • Support sales and proposals with technical scope, pricing, resource plans, and customer presentations.
  • Serve as a senior technical contact for customers, explaining engineering decisions, validation approaches, corrective actions, and recommendations.
  • Partner with Quality, Legal, and Risk to support appropriate quality systems and professional liability coverage for engineering, qualification, and validation services.

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in mechanical, chemical, biomedical, industrial engineering, or a related technical discipline.
  • At least 12 years of progressive experience delivering GMP facilities, equipment, or processes within pharmaceutical, biotechnology, advanced therapy medicinal products (ATMP), medical device, or high-containment life sciences environments.
  • At least five years leading multidisciplinary technical teams, including hiring and developing engineers and qualification personnel.
  • Deep understanding of the CQV lifecycle, including commissioning strategy, IQ/OQ/PQ, and requalification.
  • Demonstrated experience delivering CSV or CSA for GxP computerized systems.
  • Working knowledge of 21 CFR Part 11, EU GMP Annex 11, ALCOA+ principles, and data integrity expectations.
  • Experience with cleanrooms, isolators, restricted access barrier systems, biological safety cabinets, or other controlled and containment environments.
  • Experience managing third-party automation, controls, or process engineering vendors on capital projects.
  • Proven ability to establish technical processes, standards, staffing models, and delivery capabilities.
  • Prior profit-and-loss or cost-center ownership, including responsibility for budgets, utilization, and margins.
  • Strong customer communication, commercial judgment, and cross-functional leadership skills.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications and familiarity with project controls and validation lifecycle management platforms.
  • Valid driver’s license, acceptable driving record, valid passport, and ability to meet travel requirements.
  • Successful completion of a background check and drug screening.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Advanced technical degree or MBA.
  • Experience building an engineering, delivery, or validation function within an established manufacturer.
  • Field certification experience involving NSF/ANSI 49, HEPA filters, biological safety cabinets, or cleanroom classification.
  • Familiarity with certification and accreditation requirements.
  • Experience delivering modular, mobile, or prefabricated GMP facilities.
  • Experience in ATMP, cell and gene therapy, aseptic fill-finish, or hospital pharmacy compounding under USP 797/800.
  • International project experience, particularly in the Middle East or Asia-Pacific.
  • Relevant professional credentials, such as PE, PMP, CQE, CSQE, or ISPE/PDA certifications.

Physical Requirements & Working Conditions

  • Perform site inspections requiring standing, walking, kneeling, bending, reaching, and climbing ladders or stairs.
  • Work at active construction sites, in mechanical rooms, and occasionally in confined or elevated spaces.
  • Work in varying temperatures and noise levels.
  • Wear required cleanroom garments and personal protective equipment.
  • Lift and carry up to 25 pounds, with assistance for heavier items.
  • Travel by car and air, including overnight stays and extended international assignments.

Work Environment

Join a collaborative organization that values integrity, accountability, initiative, and innovation. This role offers the opportunity to build a growing technical function, develop talent, and lead complex projects that support critical regulated environments.

jobs.description:
About Megaport

We’re not your typical tech company – and we don’t want to be. Megaport is the global leader in Network as a Service (NaaS), and has transformed the way businesses connect to the cloud, data centers, and each other. We’re publicly listed on the Australian Stock Exchange and partnered with the biggest names in tech like Amazon, Microsoft, Google, Oracle, IBM, and more. Headquartered in Brisbane with a crew of over 600 people spread across Asia-Pacific, Europe, and the Americas, our employees enjoy an environment that is collaborative, supportive, and (actually) fun.

Our Team Culture

We’re a team of problem solvers, pixel pushers, code slingers, and cloud fanatics. Culture is more than a poster on the wall here – collaboration beats hierarchy, curiosity fuels our growth, and everyone’s voice matters. We take our work seriously, but not ourselves. We work across time zones to execute on our global vision, trust each other to get things done, and never compromise our values for commercial gain. Most importantly, we place our customers at the center of everything we do.
We’re committed to increasing representation in the tech industry and welcome applicants from all backgrounds. Don’t meet every requirement? That’s okay. If you’re excited about this role, we encourage you to apply.

Your Role

Megaport is growing fast, and acquisitions are a big part of our journey. We're looking for a switched-on, highly organised and action-oriented People & Culture Project Lead to help bring our businesses, people and teams together as we continue to scale globally.

This is a hands-on role for someone who loves turning complex projects into clear plans, bringing order to the chaos and, most importantly, making things happen.

Working closely with our People & Culture leadership and M&A Integration teams, you'll help drive the people side of our acquisitions - from pre-deal planning and Day 1 readiness through to making sure our new colleagues, systems and processes are successfully integrated into Megaport.

You'll work with teams across the globe, connecting the dots between People & Culture, Legal, Finance, IT and the broader business to keep integration activities on track and moving forward.

We're after someone who takes ownership, thrives on variety, isn't afraid to roll up their sleeves and knows how to get things done in a business that doesn't stand still.

We’d love to hear from you if you're energised by solving problems, juggling moving parts and seeing projects through from planning to delivery.

What You'll Be Doing

    M&A People Integration

  • Lead the planning and delivery of the people integration activities for Megaport’s acquisitions, working closely with People & Culture leadership to execute on agreed strategies.
  • Pre-acquisition planning: Support HR due diligence activities and translate identified people-related risks, obligations and priorities into actionable integration plans.
  • Day 1 Readiness: Coordinate people integration readiness ahead of acquisition completion, ensuring critical employee, payroll, systems and operational requirements are addressed.
  • Drive the delivery of people integration activities across multiple jurisdictions, ensuring agreed milestones and deliverables are achieved.
  • Develop and manage comprehensive integration project plans, including timelines, milestones, deliverables, dependencies, and responsibilities, ensuring clear accountability and timely follow-up.
  • Coordinate activities across employee onboarding and transition, employment documentation, employee data, payroll and benefits, HR systems, policies, reporting lines, communications and change management.
  • Work with internal stakeholders and external providers to coordinate the collection, validation and migration of employee information.
  • Proactively identify and manage project risks, issues and dependencies, working with stakeholders to develop practical solutions and escalating matters where necessary.
  • Prepare project updates, progress reports and other materials for People & Culture leadership and relevant stakeholders.
  • Support post-integration reviews, capturing lessons learned and identifying opportunities to improve integration processes and frameworks.
  • Develop and maintain standardised M&A people integration frameworks, templates and checklists to support consistency across future acquisitions.

    • People & Culture Projects

  • Coordinate and execute other strategic People & Culture projects across Megaport’s global operations.
  • Support initiatives to improve and standardise People & Culture systems, policies, processes and ways of working.
  • Assist with implementation of new systems, tools and operational improvements.
  • Develop project documentation, process maps, communications and supporting materials.
  • Work collaboratively with People & Culture team members to implement agreed changes and improvements

    • Stakeholder Coordination & Project Delivery

  • Build effective working relationships with stakeholders across multiple functions, countries and time zones.
  • Proactively monitor progress, manage competing priorities and dependencies, and work with stakeholders to resolve delivery challenges.
  • Maintain accurate project documentation and handle sensitive employee information appropriately.
  • Take ownership of assigned project outcomes, ensuring deliverables are completed to a high standard and within agreed timeframes.
  • Establish clear project governance and ways of working, including working sessions, action tracking, progress reporting and stakeholder communications.
  • Provide regular updates to project sponsors on progress, upcoming milestones, risks and dependencies.
  • Identify and escalate issues or decisions requiring sponsor input, providing the appropriate context and recommendations to support timely decision-making.

What We Are Looking For

    We're less interested in someone who can talk about project management frameworks and more interested in someone who knows how to make projects happen.

    You'll bring a combination of People & Culture know-how, strong project coordination skills and the confidence to work with stakeholders across a fast-moving global business.

    Experience and Qualifications

  • Approximately 4–7 years’ experience in People & Culture, HR operations, project management, business transformation or a related field.
  • Demonstrated experience coordinating and delivering projects involving multiple stakeholders and competing priorities.
  • Experience supporting M&A integration, organisational change or HR transformation projects would be highly regarded.
  • Strong understanding of HR processes and the employee lifecycle, with the ability to translate operational requirements into system workflows.
  • Demonstrated ability to coordinate complex projects or initiatives involving multiple stakeholders and competing priorities.
  • Highly organised, with strong attention to detail and the ability to manage timelines, actions and deliverables.
  • Good understanding of core People & Culture processes, including employee lifecycle management, HR systems, payroll, benefits and policies.
  • Experience working in a global or multi-jurisdictional business would be advantageous.
  • Strong proficiency in Google Workspace, with experience using HR systems.
  • Relevant qualifications in Human Resources, Business, Project Management or a related discipline would be advantageous.
  • Strong stakeholder management skills, including confidence following up on commitments and escalating risks or delays when required.
  • Sound judgement and an understanding of when matters can be progressed independently and when sponsor input or approval is required.
  • Strong problem-solving, communication and facilitation skills.
  • A proactive and adaptable approach, with the ability to work independently while maintaining appropriate visibility with project sponsors.

    • Skills & Attributes

  • Exceptional organisation: Manage details, deadlines and competing priorities so nothing falls through the cracks.
  • Ownership and accountability: Take responsibility, follow through and deliver without needing to be chased.
  • Strong execution: Translate agreed plans into action and coordinate activities through completion.
  • Problem-solving: Find practical solutions and escalate issues appropriately.
  • Communication: Keep stakeholders informed and communicate clearly and confidently.
  • Collaboration: Engage the right people and work effectively across teams.
  • Adaptability: Navigate ambiguity and changing priorities in a fast-moving business.
  • Attention to detail: Produce accurate work and respect confidentiality.
  • Continuous improvement: Look for ways to simplify and improve how we work.

What We Offer

  • Flexible working environment – a remote-first culture with coworking options available
  • Generous leave plans – including, parental leave, birthday leave, and a purchased annual leave program
  • Health and wellness support – through a wellness allowance and employee wellbeing initiatives
  • Comprehensive learning support – generous study and training allowance plus paid study leave
  • Creative, modern workspaces – designed to inspire when you're not working remotely, plus access to coworking spaces via our global WeWork membership if you work remotely, but like to get out of the house sometimes
  • Motivated, inclusive team – work alongside industry experts and fresh talent
  • Recognition programs – celebrate achievements with our Legend and Kudos award

jobs.description:
Licensed Mental Health Counselor (LMHC) $70K-85K/yr

Position Requirement: Remote Full-Time and Part-time Positions Available

If you are looking for a new opportunity to grow with a clinician founded and clinician led organization, look no further! As an authentic, unique, and skilled counselor, you have a plethora of options when it comes to work. Hospitals, community clinics, investment bank funded group practice startups, state agencies, and more.

At OptiMindHealth, we continuously strive to provide consistent, high-quality care and expand the reach of mental health care services in our communities. Unfortunately, the need often outpaces the services available to those we serve and only adds to the current mental health crisis in our nation. To combat this crisis and further our mission, we need more compassionate and skilled clinicians to join our cause. We are not interested in the “burnt-out” clinician that no longer finds meaning in their work and is just going through the motions; we are seeking people with a passion to provide excellent care, and the belief that we, together, can make a difference. If that’s you, then you’re in the right place!

Our approach with our team is simple, we take care of you, the clinician, so you can take care of patients. How do we do that? By investing in your growth, supporting you financially, holistically, and professionally, while being flexible regarding your personal needs and goals. The work we do with patients is hard enough and over the years we have found that our team often does their best work when the administrative burdens are taken off their plate and they are able to be fully present with their patients. Our administrative support team handles all non-clinical tasks so that you don’t have to think about anything except focusing on your patients.

Why bother with the endless administrative burdens and isolation of private practice? Use your highly trained interpersonal skills to change the culture around mental health care, decrease stigma, and help people who need you, while being supported by an experienced multi-disciplinary team of clinicians. Let us take care of the rest!

Want to work part time? No problem. Want to do group therapy? Sure! Want to do long-term psychodynamic psychotherapy with all of your clients? We do it every day. Interested in treating couples? We can make that happen. Basically, what we are saying is that whatever outpatient care you are interested in providing, we can surely accommodate you. We know you have exceptional skills; we want you to be part of our team.

The perfect candidate will share our passion for improving and expanding access to high quality mental health care and will thrive in a culture that emphasizes creativity, authenticity, humor, compassion, acceptance, and determination. Telehealth or onsite, we support your authentic and unique growth trajectory, while being yourself and having some fun!

We prioritize the clinician's experience by offering excellent compensation, benefits, training/supervision, and flexibility. Whether you’re working from home or in one of our physical offices, if you’re doing it during your scheduled work hours, you’re getting paid for it. Our compensation packages include:

  • Starting Salary range: $70,000.00 - $85,000.00 per year.
  • 401K with maximum employee matching.
  • Health care benefits.
  • Generous paid vacation and sick leave time.
  • Paid administrative time for consultation, supervision, and documentation.
  • Full administrative support.

Here are a few extra perks our team loves:

  • Paid supervision, clinical rounds, and administrative time.
  • Customized schedules within available clinic hours.
  • Hybrid work environment if desired: Telehealth and/or in-person (in select locations).
  • Muti-disciplinary team approach to treatment.
  • Incredible administrative support team.
  • Company leadership that understands the practice of mental healthcare.
  • Inclusive, socially responsible, client focused leadership.
  • We are not a franchise or a big investor-backed company.
  • And most importantly, clinician-led and clinician-FOCUSED!

We know what it’s like to work in an organization led by businesspeople instead of clinicians. We, on the other hand, have organically grown as a socially responsible company that started as a single provider on a mission to destigmatize and broaden the reach of mental health care, to an integrated and holistic group of exceptional providers with diverse backgrounds working toward that mission. We are fortunate to have significantly increased the reach of mental health care services in our communities, and look forward to continuing to provide consistent, high-quality care to those we serve for many years to come.

We will rely on your expertise to:

  • Evaluate mental health conditions, diagnose, create, and implement a treatment plan, complete ongoing documentation including further diagnosis, treatment plan reviews, and case notes according to company policy.
  • Provide excellent care for clients and collaborate with a dynamic team to further the mission of filling gaps in our community.
  • Utilize creativity in interventions to help clients achieve and exceed goals.
  • Prepare and submit individual documentation for each session per company guidelines and protocol. 
  • For Full-Time status, clinicians must maintain at least 32 available hours for patient care per week.
  • Coordinate services with other care providers, families, work personnel, medical personnel, other OptiMindHealth staff, and school staff as needed.
  • Attend and participate in all clinical staff meetings and trainings.

Qualifications and Skill for This Positions: 

  • Master's degree in one of the behavioral sciences or related fields from an accredited college/university.
  • Full, current, unrestricted license to practice independently (LMHC, LCSW, LMFT) is required.
  • Experience with electronic health records and completing clinical documentation.
  • Effective written and verbal communication skills.
  • Experience and willingness to work collaboratively and creatively to meet necessary deadlines.
  • Comfort and familiarity working with clients with a diverse range of problems or concerns. 
  • Ability to pass a background check in a way that confirms to us you can provide safe care.  
  • Demonstrate and model stable and appropriate boundaries with clients.

Additionally Valuable (but not essential) Qualifications for This Position: 

  • Experience working in community, group, or private practice mental health.
  • Currently paneled or credentialed with insurance network.
  • Multilingual or bilingual proficiency.
  • Specialty area of practice. 

We can’t wait to hear your story and look forward to sharing ours!

WHO ARE WE?

Launch Potato is the discovery and conversion company. We reach tens of millions of people every month through our brands, including FinanceBuzz, All About Cookies, and OnlyInYourState. We turn that attention into real outcomes for our partners, some of the world's leading companies.

Our mission: create predictable, high-value customer acquisition at scale by connecting discovery, intent, and performance across category-leading consumer brands in finance, travel, and entertainment.

We run profitable and bootstrapped, with a South Florida HQ and a remote-first team across 18 countries.

WHY JOIN US?

You own outcomes here, not tasks. We measure work by impact, not activity. The pace is real, and change is constant, so the people who do best turn change into opportunity instead of waiting for it to settle. Feedback runs direct and lands with respect. Ordinary people make themselves extraordinary at Launch Potato.

YOUR ROLE

You'll build the models that decide which carrier each auto insurance shopper sees on our click wall. The goal is to send every user to the carrier most likely to convert them, so carriers see our traffic convert and raise their bids. You'll also own the buying models behind our media spend, which are held to ROAS.

Carrier conversion data (quotes, policies and acquisition cost) is now coming back to us, and you'll be the one who puts it to work in production. The hard part is the data. Outcomes land weeks or months after the click, many sessions are sparse, the same shoppers come back, and the market drifts. Our bids also decide which users we win, so the model shapes the data it learns from next.

This is a hands-on individual contributor role. You frame problems directly with the business, find your own data, build and validate the model, and stay with it through deployment and monitoring. An ML engineer works alongside you on the production side. Auto insurance takes most of your time to start, and scope broadens to other verticals over time.

We're remote first, and most of the company works East Coast hours.

WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

By day 60, you run our insurance marketplace media buying on your own.

By the end of your first year:

  • Click wall serving that matches each user to the right carrier
  • Carrier conversion data running in production models
  • Automated marketplace bidding taken from proof of concept to scale
  • A clear approach for repeat users and sparse sessions
  • Production models that hold up through drift and changing objectives
  • Output the business trusts and uses without rework

MUST HAVE

  • 5+ years of hands-on applied data science with measurable business impact
  • Your models drove paid media decisions: spend, bidding or ad serving. Attribution and reporting alone don't qualify.
  • You built what's on your resume and can explain it down to the loss function and architecture choice, neural network fundamentals included
  • You see how today's bids shape tomorrow's training data, and you've handled late labels, sparse features or drift
  • You own models end to end: you find your own data, build through deployment and monitoring, and bring a point of view
  • Expert Python and SQL

NICE TO HAVES

  • Real ad budget spent in live auctions
  • Large-scale ranking or recommendation systems
  • Explaining tradeoffs to non-technical partners in plain terms
  • Designing for auction feedback loops, selection bias and exploration
  • Hands-on neural network work, such as embeddings of text, creative or user behavior
  • AWS for data science: ECS, S3, Athena, SageMaker
  • CI/CD deployment

Title

Partnership and Resource Mobilisation Coordinator

Reports To

Programmes Manager

Status

FTE 0.8 - 4 days per week

Location

Remote working, based in The Netherlands, Germany or the United Kingdom.

You must have the right to work in the country for which you apply. IDC is unable to support work visa applications or relocation.

Languages

Excellent communication skills in oral and written English

Compensation

Per annum depending on skills and experience:

  • €36,000 to €42,400 gross annually for 0.8 FTE (based on a full-time equivalent of €45,000 to €53,000)

Background

International Detention Coalition (IDC) is a unique global network of over 200 civil society organisations and individuals in more than 75 countries, which coordinates with members and partners on advocacy, research, coalition and capacity building, to eliminate immigration detention and advance rights-based alternatives to detention. IDC is a highly recognised, impact-driven organisation, offering a stimulating workplace committed to local, national, regional and global change.

Role Purpose

The Partnership and Resource Mobilisation Coordinator supports the development and implementation of IDC’s fundraising and resource mobilisation efforts, helping to strengthen and diversify the organisation’s funding base, with a focus on mobilising private capital and securing funding from donors and sectors that IDC has not yet reached.

Role Summary

The Partnership and Resource Mobilisation Coordinator combines strategic thinking with hands-on implementation, and works to identify and pursue funding opportunities, develop high-quality pitches, support donor communications, coordinate with relevant team members, and maintain strong relationships between IDC and its funders, and prospective funders. Working closely with the Executive Director, Programmes Manager, Chief Communications Officer, as well as the finance and regional programme teams, the Partnership and Resource Mobilisation Coordinator will help ensure that fundraising is proactive, coordinated, innovative and aligned with IDC’s organisational strategy and programme priorities.

The Partnership and Resource Mobilisation Coordinator will help strengthen IDC’s long-term financial sustainability by building a proactive, relationship-driven and diversified fundraising function. The role will focus on mobilising private philanthropic capital, engaging philanthropic and entrepreneurial networks, and developing strategic relationships with prospective supporters, particularly from sectors that IDC has not yet reached. In parallel, the Coordinator will explore innovative funding approaches and emerging giving channels, translating promising opportunities into meaningful, long-term partnerships that expand and diversify IDC’s funding base.

Role Responsibilities

Strategic Relationship Development & Engagement

  • Support the development and implementation of IDC’s organisational fundraising and resource mobilisation strategy, ensuring that all activities align with IDC’s ethical guidelines and policies.
  • Maintain an overview of IDC’s funding priorities, funding needs and development pipeline.
  • Support forward planning of fundraising opportunities, including prospecting, cultivation, proposal development and renewal timelines.
  • Monitor developments in the funding environment, particularly related to the mobilisation of private capital and identify emerging opportunities, trends and risks relevant to IDC.
  • Contribute to organisational discussions about funding priorities, positioning and sustainability.
  • Identify opportunities to strengthen and diversify IDC’s funding base, in particular:
    • Mobilise private philanthropic capital Identify and develop opportunities with corporates, philanthropists, family offices, donor-advised funds (DAFs) and other private funding partners to broaden and diversify IDC’s funding base.
    • Explore innovative funding approaches Identify and assess emerging funding channels and mechanisms, for example, digital giving and crypto philanthropy, that could unlock new sources of support for IDC.
    • Develop impact-oriented partnerships Build relationships with funders and partners who share IDC’s mission and are interested in supporting measurable, long-term social change through strategic, mission-aligned partnerships.

Donor Cultivation and Communication

  • Champion networking and relationship-building opportunities that strengthen the organisation’s profile, partnerships and reach.
  • Coordinate follow-up, such as thank you letters and other stewardship communications, with funders and prospective funders, ensuring actions and opportunities are appropriately tracked.
  • Prepare background research, briefing materials and correspondence for donor meetings.
  • Liaise with the Executive Director, Programmes Manager and relevant team members on potential opportunities related to target funders.
  • Coordinate relevant IDC impact stories and social media activities in cooperation with the Chief Communications Officer.

Development Research and Prospecting

  • Conduct research into new prospective funders as described above, from sectors we have not yet reached, that match IDC’s strategy and priorities, while respecting IDC’s ethical guidelines and policies.
  • Oversee and maintain a comprehensive funder database and assess prospective opportunities against IDC’s strategic priorities, programmes, and organisational capacity in consultation with relevant personnel.
  • Update IDC’s Executive Director, Programmes Manager and relevant personnel regularly by preparing concise prospect profiles and recommendations for internal consideration.
  • Develop and maintain a pipeline of prospective funding opportunities.

Funding Cultivation

  • Coordinate and contribute to the development of high-quality concept notes, proposals, pitch decks, and tailored partnership propositions for different types of prospective supporters, in collaboration with IDC’s Executive Director and relevant personnel.
  • Work with IDC colleagues, including the Chief Communications Officer to translate IDC’s mission, strategic priorities, programmes and approach into compelling and impact-oriented funding propositions, incorporating outcomes from impact monitoring and assessment, such as impact stories that resonate with funders’ interests and priorities.
  • Coordinate proposal development processes related to the mobilisation of private capital, including timelines, inputs, review and submission.
  • Maintain a forward-looking calendar of funding opportunities, applications, pitches and renewals.

Development Systems and MEL

  • Maintain and improve systems for tracking prospects, opportunities, applications, funder relationships and development activity.
  • Contribute to regular development reporting and pipeline reviews.
  • Track fundraising progress against agreed objectives and priorities.
  • Capture and share learning from successful and unsuccessful funding approaches.
  • Contribute to improving organisational fundraising tools, templates, processes and resources.

Collaboration and Teamwork

  • Work with relevant team members to develop and maintain a system for grant administration and acquisition, including development of resources and capacity building for IDC team members.
  • Work collaboratively with relevant team members, including the Executive Director, Programmes Manager, Chief Communications Officer, as well as the finance and regional programme teams to achieve fundraising goals and objectives.
  • Participate in team meetings, training sessions and other organisational activities as needed.

Core Responsibilities

  • Actively contribute to a culture of agile learning, collaboration, teamwork and support within the IDC team.
  • Demonstrate passion and alignment with IDC’s mission, vision and core values of innovation, collaboration, respect, inclusion, representation and being solutions-focused.
  • Demonstrate an understanding of IDC policies to ensure a positive and safe working environment for all.
  • Actively engage with organisational systems, processes and infrastructure to ensure sustainability and appropriate safeguarding of institutional knowledge, assets and core activities over time.
  • Test and use AI tools across relevant areas of work, where appropriate, to enhance efficiency, effectiveness and innovation.

Essential Qualifications

  • Relevant degree in management, business administration, economics, social sciences, communications, marketing or related field or equivalent professional experience.
  • Proven experience and a successful track record in fundraising or development and mobilisation of private capital for the non-profit sector.
  • Strategic and entrepreneurial mindset and the ability to recognise opportunities, think creatively, work proactively and develop new approaches to building partnerships and diversifying income.
  • Experience maintaining funding pipelines, donor information or similar relationship-management systems.
  • Knowledge of fundraising best practices and grant regulations
  • Ability to understand complex organisational or programme information and translate it into clear, compelling pitches.
  • Demonstrated understanding of the issues faced by refugees, people seeking asylum and migrants, particularly those affected by immigration detention.
  • Strong research, analytical and writing skills in English.
  • Excellent networking and relationship-building skills.
  • Excellent organisational skills including attention to detail, with the ability to multitask and prioritise effectively and work within time constraints and competing deadlines.
  • Ability to work independently and proactively in a remote and internationally distributed team.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite, donor management software, online research tools and relevant AI technologies.
  • Commitment to the mission and values of IDC.
  • Ability to travel if needed.

Desireable

  • Experience engaging with private philanthropists, corporate giving, family foundations, family offices, major donors, donor-advised funds (DAFs), philanthropic advisers or other private funding networks.
  • Familiarity with entrepreneurial networks, business angels or other intermediaries who can facilitate access to philanthropic capital.
  • Experience exploring alternative funding channels, such as digital giving, crypto philanthropy or other emerging approaches to resource mobilisation.
  • An established professional network in philanthropy, private giving, business development or related fields, or the ability to build such networks proactively.
  • Understanding of impact-oriented philanthropy and the ability to communicate the social impact of an organisation in ways that resonate with prospective supporters.
  • Knowledge of the Spanish language.
  • Knowledge of project management/fundraising software such as Salesforce, Sales Navigator, etc.

Application Process

To apply for this role, please upload your resume and a cover letter on IDC Careers’ Webpage, by Friday 6 November 2026. Please ensure that you clearly address all of the key selection criteria in your application.

If you have enquiries, please write to . Please note that applications will not be accepted if sent by email.

Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted. The selected candidate will be expected to start as soon as possible.

NB: All applications must be submitted in English.

We envision a world where immigration detention no longer exists. And we work with everyone to make that vision a reality. We believe people should be able to live freely while they await the outcome of their immigration case, and we advocate for the human rights and dignity of everyone impacted by immigration detention.

IDC is solutions-focused, meaning that we work with lived experience leaders, governments, decision-makers, civil society, UN agencies and other actors to deliver alternatives that benefit migrants, communities and society at large. We are truly global, uniting a coalition of civil society organisations, community groups and individuals from all over the world. While the movement spans continents, we all have a clear purpose: to reduce and ultimately end immigration detention and to promote alternatives.

IDC values diversity, equality and inclusivity. Applications are welcome from all backgrounds. We especially encourage applications of those from underrepresented backgrounds, including but not limited to gender, race, age, sexual orientation, disability and religion. In particular, we highly encourage leaders with lived experience of the impacts of detention to apply. If potential candidates require any adaptations to usual recruitment processes, please do not hesitate to note this in your application.

Salary: €36,000 to €42,400 gross annually for 0.8 FTE (based on a full-time equivalent of €45,000 to €53,000)

jobs.description:
About Nebius:

Nebius is leading a new era in cloud infrastructure for the global AI economy. We are building a full-stack AI cloud platform that supports developers and enterprises from data and model training through to production deployment, without the cost and complexity of building large in-house AI/ML infrastructure.

Built by engineers, for engineers. From large-scale GPU orchestration to inference optimization, we own the hard problems across compute, storage, networking and applied AI.

Listed on Nasdaq (NBIS) and headquartered in Amsterdam, we have a global footprint with R&D hubs across Europe, the UK, North America and Israel. Our team of 1,500+ includes hundreds of engineers with deep expertise across hardware, software and AI R&D.

The role

We run a large-scale GPU cloud and AI infrastructure platform. Fraud and abuse — stolen payment cards, fake sign-ups, compute mining, credential abuse, and coordinated free-tier exploitation — directly threaten platform economics, capacity availability for legitimate customers, and our standing with payment providers and cloud partners.

As Product Manager, Anti-Fraud, you own the product roadmap for the systems that detect, prevent, and respond to fraud and abuse across the customer lifecycle — from onboarding and payment through to ongoing consumption. You sit at the intersection of Trust & Safety, Payments/Billing, Risk, Data Science, and Product Engineering, and you balance two goals in constant tension: stop bad actors and keep friction near zero for real customers.

Your responsibilities will include:

  • Own the end-to-end anti-fraud product roadmap: signup/KYC checks, payment fraud detection, account takeover protection, and compute-abuse (e.g., crypto mining, resource reselling) prevention.
  • Own the rules and risk-scoring surfaces — the tooling that lets analysts and data scientists define, test, and deploy detection rules and ML models with clear guardrails and audit trails.
  • Own the manual review and case-management experience for the Trust & Safety operations team, including queues, evidence views, and action workflows (block, limit, step-up verification, release).
  • Own customer-facing friction points — verification flows, step-up challenges, and appeals — designed to minimize false positives and protect the legitimate user experience.
  • Identify fraud and abuse incidents early — define the signals, alerts, and thresholds that surface incidents before they scale, and own the detection surface that flags them.
  • Participate in incident reviews and post-mortems, capturing root causes and turning each finding into concrete improvements to detection rules, models, and the roadmap.
  • Ensure timely response to active incidents — drive fast triage, clear ownership, and mitigation, working alongside Trust & Safety, Engineering, and Data Science to contain impact.
  • Write clear PRDs and specs that translate fuzzy risk problems into shippable engineering and data-science work.
  • Partner with Analytics team on detection models — defining the problem, labels, and success criteria, and deciding where rules vs. ML are the right tool.
  • Run experiments and monitor rollouts, watching both fraud-catch metrics and false-positive / customer-friction impact.
  • Work with Legal/Compliance to keep detection and enforcement aligned with payment-network rules, KYC/AML expectations, and data-privacy requirements.
  • Track and report on fraud loss, chargeback rate, false-positive rate, review throughput, and time-to-detection.

We expect you to have:

  • Proven product management experience in fraud, risk, trust & safety, or payments.
  • Strong analytical skills — comfortable with data, SQL or equivalent, and reasoning about precision/recall trade-offs and metrics.
  • Ability to make decisions under ambiguity and to balance security, business, and customer-experience priorities.
  • Solid collaboration with engineering and data science; you can hold a technical conversation about signals, features, and model behavior.
  • Exposure to cloud, SaaS, marketplace, fintech, or infrastructure products.
  • Understanding payment fraud, chargebacks, KYC/AML, or device/network signals (fingerprinting, velocity, IP reputation).

It would be an added bonus if you have:

  • Familiarity with ML-based detection systems and their operational lifecycle (drift, retraining, monitoring).
  • Experience with abuse patterns specific to compute or GPU platforms (mining, credential stuffing, free-tier farming).

Benefits & Perks:

  • Competitive compensation
  • Career growth and learning opportunities
  • Flexibility and ownership
  • Collaborative and innovative culture
  • Opportunity to work on impactful AI projects
  • International environment and talented teams

What's it like to work at Nebius:

Fast moving - Bold thinking - Constant growth - Meaningful impact - Trust and real ownership - Opportunity to shape the future of AI

jobs.excerpt: Who we areSamsara (NYSE: IOT) is the pioneer of the Connected Operations™ Cloud, which is a platform that enables organizations that depend on physical operations to harness Internet of Things (IoT) data to develop actionable insights and improve their operations.
jobs.description:
Who we are

Samsara (NYSE: IOT) is the pioneer of the Connected Operations™ Cloud, which is a platform that enables organizations that depend on physical operations to harness Internet of Things (IoT) data to develop actionable insights and improve their operations. At Samsara, we are helping improve the safety, efficiency and sustainability of the physical operations that power our global economy. Representing more than 40% of global GDP, these industries are the infrastructure of our planet, including agriculture, construction, field services, transportation, and manufacturing — and we are excited to help digitally transform their operations at scale.

Working at Samsara means you’ll help define the future of physical operations and be on a team that’s shaping an exciting array of product solutions, including Video-Based Safety, Vehicle Telematics, Apps and Driver Workflows, and Equipment Monitoring. As part of a recently public company, you’ll have the autonomy and support to make an impact as we build for the long term.

About the role:

Samsara's Customer Success team is on the front lines of business value delivery by helping customers adopt our platform, realize measurable business value, and renew and expand with confidence. Billing errors, concession requests, and cancellation or return exceptions currently land with CSMs, CS managers, and several partner teams, each holding part of the picture. As our customer base and billing complexity have grown, these cases take too long, repeat for the same reasons, and pull CSMs away from adoption and renewal work. As the Contract and Billing Resolution Specialist, you will be the single owner of complex billing and contract cases for Mid-Market and Commercial accounts.

You will take a customer's report that something is wrong with their bill, work out what happened across systems and teams, choose the right path to fix it, and see it through, keeping the customer informed. It is part detective, part project manager, part customer advocate. You will also tell the teams who own the underlying systems and processes what keeps breaking.

Your role will be cross-functional, working alongside and connecting Customer Success Managers, Sales, Billing Support, Order-to-Cash, Sales Ops, Deal Desk, Finance, and Legal. This is a new role, and you will help shape the case record, the root-cause tags, and the monthly read-out that define how Customer Success resolves billing and contract cases at Samsara.

This is a remote position open to candidates residing in the US except the San Francisco Bay Metro Area, NYC Metro Area, and Washington, D.C. Metro Area. Relocation assistance will not be provided for this role.

You should apply if:

  • You want to impact the industries that run our world: Every phone call you answer and every email you send can affect whether truck drivers deliver goods on time and without accidents, whether students get dropped off safely from school, or whether power gets restored quickly after a natural disaster.
  • You thrive the most when solving problems: Our constantly expanding technology and the complexities faced by our customers provide an exciting range of challenges for our Customer Success teams. With a growth mindset and a desire to learn, you will strategically partner with our customers to find unique solutions to help keep their operations safe, efficient, and sustainable.
  • You are a natural relationship builder: Whether the relationship is with our customers or with cross-functional teams in Samsara, you are in constant communication and collaboration with key stakeholders to win as a team.
  • You are the architect of your own career: If you put in the work, this role won’t be your last at Samsara. This Customer Success team is still shaping its future and you will have plenty of autonomy and opportunities to master your craft in a hyper growth environment.
  • You want to be with the best: At Samsara, we win together, celebrate together and support each other. You will be surrounded by the best and brightest professionals out there.

In this role, you will:

  • Own complex billing and contract cases for Mid-Market and Commercial accounts, from the first report to a confirmed fix, and keep the customer informed in plain terms, including accounts that are delinquent or facing suspension.
  • Reconstruct the full story behind a billing error across contracts, order forms, segment or ownership changes, reprocessing, and invoicing, including cases with several AE handoffs and no clean record of what was promised.
  • Separate a correction of a Samsara error from a concession, a return, a reprocess, and a contract amendment, and choose the path that fixes the customer's billing, not only the immediate complaint.
  • Drive Billing Support, Order-to-Cash, Sales Ops, Deal Desk, Finance, and Legal to execute the fix.
  • Evaluate and prepare concession requests: confirm whether Samsara was at fault, size the request against policy and the approval matrix, write a short case summary (what happened, root cause, options considered and ruled out, recommendation, and risk), route it to the right approver, and confirm the credit is applied and the customer told.
  • Support cancellation, return, and ETF exceptions: validate eligibility (purchase and renewal dates, trial history, Return ACV, financing partner, documentation), prepare the case for the approving team, act as the Customer Success fallback when the first approver does not respond within the window, and make sure approved outcomes are processed.
  • Be the front door for billing, concession, and cancellation requests: log every request in a single case record, including those that arrive via Slack, email, or Gainsight; redirect them to the right path; and coach CSMs and AEs on what a complete request looks like.
  • Fix repeat causes: tag the root cause on every case, separate one-offs from systemic failures, and deliver a monthly read-out to the teams that own the systems and processes involved.
  • Carry forward the billing improvement work with Support, Finance, and Product, including earlier detection of billing problems that threaten renewals.
  • Champion, role model, and embed Samsara's operating principles, including Keep a High Bar, Be Intellectually Honest, and Solve Problems Together, as we scale.

Minimum requirements for the role:

  • 4+ years of experience in billing operations, order to cash, revenue operations, deal desk, contracts, or a similar finance and operations role.
  • This is a demanding position with high internal visibility that requires strong priority management and high emotional intelligence.
  • Strong investigative skills: you can rebuild a timeline from incomplete or conflicting information across CRM, billing, and contract systems, including when the people involved have left.
  • Sound financial judgment about credits, concessions, reprocessing, and refunds, and a clear way of explaining your recommendation.
  • Customer-facing communication that stays honest and composed in hard conversations, and written summaries a leader can read once and decide on.
  • A record of driving results across teams without authority over them, including working to deadlines in an approval process.
  • Familiarity with order forms, amendments, and terms, and how they flow into billing.
  • Comfort with ambiguity and incomplete precedent, and rigorous case management so nothing drops across weeks and stakeholders.
  • Diplomacy, tact, and poise under pressure when working through customer issues.

An ideal candidate also has:

  • Experience handling escalated or high-dollar billing disputes.
  • Experience with Salesforce, NetSuite, or an equivalent ERP, and CPQ tools. We also use Zendesk, Gainsight, and Sweethawk.
  • Customer Success, Support, or account management background with customer-facing financial or contract work.
  • Experience building or improving billing dispute processes.
  • Exposure to subscription or hardware-plus-subscription billing.
  • AI First: Experience using AI tooling to drive efficiency and outcomes.
  • Strong bias for action and insistence on high standards

Total Rewards

At Samsara, we build for the people who keep the global economy moving. We want owners, not passengers, which is why our rewards are designed to fuel high-impact builders. Our compensation program delivers above-market total compensation through a combination of base salary, performance-based bonus/variable pay, and equity (for eligible roles) in a high-growth public company. We meaningfully differentiate pay for our top performers, who have the opportunity to earn above-market compensation that can outpace the broader market over time.

Beyond compensation, we provide the foundations that enable long-term success: a flexible, employee-led remote model, a professional development stipend, comprehensive health and parental leave plans, and more. If you’re ready to build for the long term and own the outcome, your journey starts here.

Flexible Working

At Samsara, we embrace a flexible working model that caters to the diverse needs of our teams. Our offices are open for those who prefer to work in-person and we also support remote work where it aligns with our operational requirements. For certain positions, being close to one of our offices or within a specific geographic area is important to facilitate collaboration, access to resources, or alignment with our service regions. In these cases, the job description will clearly indicate any working location requirements. Our goal is to ensure that all members of our team can contribute effectively, whether they are working on-site, in a hybrid model, or fully remotely. All offers of employment are contingent upon an individual’s ability to secure and maintain the legal right to work at the company and in the specified work location, if applicable.

Belonging at Samsara

At Samsara, we welcome everyone regardless of their background. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, sex, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, protected veteran status, disability, age, and other characteristics protected by law. We depend on the unique approaches of our team members to help us solve complex problems and want to ensure that Samsara is a place where people from all backgrounds can make an impact.

Accommodations

Samsara is an inclusive work environment, and we are committed to ensuring equal opportunity in employment for qualified persons with disabilities. Please email or click here if you require any reasonable accommodations throughout the recruiting process.

Our Commitment to Authenticity

OMH offers a variety of part-time and/or full-time options to our clinicians. Packages can be customized towards every clinician’s needs. Join a leading clinician-led behavioral health company today! OptiMindHealth (OMH) is expanding and seeking compassionate psychotherapists to join our team and work remotely from the comfort of their home. Today, OMH provides superior behavioral health services patients in Massachusetts and Colorado. Since 2016, we’ve specialized in serving both adult and adolescent patients in a supportive outpatient environment. Our practice strives to improve access to holistic and cost-effective mental health care while supporting our clinical staff in all aspects of their work. Our clinicians define this work as the perfect balance between flexibility and efficiency.

Packages can include some combination of:

· Competitive Salary

· Medical benefits

· Paid malpractice policy

· CEU reimbursement

· Paid time off (PTO) and paid holidays

· Productivity Bonuses in select areas

· Work-Life Balance

· Flexible Work Schedule

· Remote work environment

  • No extra "on call" work, simply cover the care for your own patients!

It is common for clinicians to diversify their work today. Therefore, OMH’s "work from home" and part-time options are the perfect complement to your professional and/or personal commitments. You can feel secure that OMH will offer steady, consistent income throughout your tenure.

Work from or close to home:

With locations in Colorado and Massachusetts, OMH is continuing to expand into states around the country. OMH will work with you to identify the best “fit” and will provide everything you need to treat OMH patients remotely from the comfort of your home. Our interview process focuses on your skill sets, interest as well as geographic location to match you to the best available option to begin working with OMH. Ask to speak with our recruitment team today to identify the local office(s) in your area, as well as those offices that are being planned for launch. Of course, if you prefer to work from home, we also have fully remote positions available.

Responsibilities:

The psychotherapist will participate in the integrated care team model at OMH. Outpatient behavioral health practices like OMH are getting more attention than ever before due to the emphasis on team approaches. Join OMH to perfect your skills in the emerging field of integrated behavioral health care. The interdisciplinary health care team includes physicians, psychiatric nurse practitioners, licensed clinical psychologists, and licensed mental health professionals (LCSW/LPC/LMFT/LMHC). OMH values clinical relationships between all provider levels and believes this coordinated, collaborative approach provides the highest level of care to the patients we are privileged to serve.

Customize the care for each patient:

Our clinicians have the unique ability to customize the care for each and every individual patient. You will have the autonomy to determine how often you see a patient as well as the appropriate length of time spent with each patient. Individual psychotherapy is the most common clinical work performed, but our clinicians also perform family therapy, group therapy, and psychological testing as needed and/or appropriate to a wide range of presenting problems of our patients.

Pick your own schedule!

  • Enjoy the freedom to create your own custom schedules with the perfect work/life balance.
  • Typically, clinicians work between Mondays – Fridays somewhere between the hours of 7:00 AM – 7:00 PM.

Focus on the patient’s care without the hassle or any additional on-call responsibilities. Simply cover the care for you own patients! Our psychotherapists focus on the patient’s care and our back-office support team handles the rest. This allows our clinicians time to be spent where it should be; with the patients they serve. Each clinician is responsible for clinical care and documentation following treatment sessions. Once that’s complete, our support team will handle all billing, collections, credentialing, etc. Once you leave the office for the day, your time is yours. No additional "on-call" responsibilities and no time spent wasted dealing with insurance companies.

Interested in benefits?

Full-time clinicians are eligible to participate for medical health benefits. Please speak with the recruitment team to obtain additional specifics on benefits.

Leadership & Advancement:

OMH is a growing, clinician-led company. Our Site Supervisors are geographically dispersed throughout the areas we work in order to have staff leaders available to every clinician. Talk with our recruitment team today about the advancement opportunities to become senior psychotherapists and/or site supervisors.

Education & Licensure:

Completion of an accredited program with certification and licensure as a Licensed Mental Health Professional (LPC/LMFT/LCSW/LMHC) in the state of Arizona is required, with the ability to practice independently.

Licensure in the state(s) of Massachusetts and/or Colorado preferred.

The specific statements shown in each section of this Job Description are not intended to be all-inclusive. They represent typical elements and criteria considered necessary to perform the job successfully. The job’s responsibilities/tasks may be modified and/or expanded over time. OMH will inform the employee when changes in the respective job description are made.

Job Summary
We are seeking an experienced Embedded Semiconductor Engineer to design and build software tooling, firmware, and infrastructure that support semiconductor design, verification, manufacturing, and post-silicon validation. In this role you will partner with hardware engineers and EDA teams to build software that accelerates silicon development cycles and improves yield, performance, and quality. The ideal candidate will combine strong software engineering fundamentals with practical experience working alongside hardware teams in EDA, verification, or post-silicon environments. In this role you will work closely with cross-functional partners — product, design, engineering, operations, and business stakeholders — to translate ambiguous requirements into well-engineered solutions, and will be expected to raise the bar through code review, design review, and mentorship of more junior engineers. The successful candidate brings strong engineering discipline, a clear communication style, and a track record of shipping meaningful work that holds up well in production.

  • Mentor and coach junior and mid-level engineers through code review, design review, pair programming, and structured knowledge sharing, helping the broader team grow in technical maturity and confidence over time.
  • Continuously evaluate emerging hardware platforms and toolchains, assessing maturity, fit for purpose, and total cost of ownership, and make grounded recommendations on which to adopt, pilot, or defer based on real engineering needs.

  • Six or more years of software engineering experience, with significant time in semiconductor environments.
  • Strong programming skills in C, C++, and Python.
  • Hands-on experience with EDA, verification, or post-silicon validation workflows.
  • Solid understanding of hardware-software interaction at a low level.
  • Experience building large-scale compute infrastructure (grid, cloud, HPC).

jobs.description:
WHO ARE WE?

Launch Potato is the discovery and conversion company. We reach tens of millions of people every month through our brands, including FinanceBuzz, All About Cookies, and OnlyInYourState. We turn that attention into real outcomes for our partners, some of the world's leading companies.

Our mission: create predictable, high-value customer acquisition at scale by connecting discovery, intent, and performance across category-leading consumer brands in finance, travel, and entertainment.

We run profitable and bootstrapped, with a South Florida HQ and a remote-first team across 18 countries.

WHY JOIN US?

You own outcomes here, not tasks. We measure work by impact, not activity. The pace is real, and change is constant, so the people who do best turn change into opportunity instead of waiting for it to settle. Feedback runs direct and lands with respect. Ordinary people make themselves extraordinary at Launch Potato.

YOUR ROLE

You'll build the models that decide which carrier each auto insurance shopper sees on our click wall. The goal is to send every user to the carrier most likely to convert them, so carriers see our traffic convert and raise their bids. You'll also own the buying models behind our media spend, which are held to ROAS.

Carrier conversion data (quotes, policies and acquisition cost) is now coming back to us, and you'll be the one who puts it to work in production. The hard part is the data. Outcomes land weeks or months after the click, many sessions are sparse, the same shoppers come back, and the market drifts. Our bids also decide which users we win, so the model shapes the data it learns from next.

This is a hands-on individual contributor role. You frame problems directly with the business, find your own data, build and validate the model, and stay with it through deployment and monitoring. An ML engineer works alongside you on the production side. Auto insurance takes most of your time to start, and scope broadens to other verticals over time.

We're remote first, and most of the company works East Coast hours.

WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

By day 60, you run our insurance marketplace media buying on your own.

By the end of your first year:

  • Click wall serving that matches each user to the right carrier
  • Carrier conversion data running in production models
  • Automated marketplace bidding taken from proof of concept to scale
  • A clear approach for repeat users and sparse sessions
  • Production models that hold up through drift and changing objectives
  • Output the business trusts and uses without rework

MUST HAVE

  • 5+ years of hands-on applied data science with measurable business impact
  • Your models drove paid media decisions: spend, bidding or ad serving. Attribution and reporting alone don't qualify.
  • You built what's on your resume and can explain it down to the loss function and architecture choice, neural network fundamentals included
  • You see how today's bids shape tomorrow's training data, and you've handled late labels, sparse features or drift
  • You own models end to end: you find your own data, build through deployment and monitoring, and bring a point of view
  • Expert Python and SQL

NICE TO HAVES

  • Real ad budget spent in live auctions
  • Large-scale ranking or recommendation systems
  • Explaining tradeoffs to non-technical partners in plain terms
  • Designing for auction feedback loops, selection bias and exploration
  • Hands-on neural network work, such as embeddings of text, creative or user behavior
  • AWS for data science: ECS, S3, Athena, SageMaker
  • CI/CD deployment
