Solutions Engineer, Pre-Sales (West)

Sales Engineering | United States (Remote) — Pacific, Mountain or Central Region

You'll be the technical lead on Alkira deals — in the room with network architects and infrastructure directors, owning the technical side of the deal from first conversation through POC to close. You'll do that as part of an experienced Sales Engineering team, with senior SEs alongside you on the largest and most complex opportunities.

This is a pre-sales engineering role. You'll partner directly with an Account Manager on strategy and carry real influence over what we build next — our Product team treats SE field feedback as a primary input to the roadmap. It's also a role you can grow in: you'll have senior SEs to learn from, and a clear path for career growth.

Location: Remote, US. Candidates should reside in the Pacific, Mountain or Central time zone for territory coverage.

Travel: approximately 25%, including regional air travel as needed. Please discuss the specifics for this position with the recruiter.

What you'll do

  • Present and demo the Alkira platform to technical decision makers, from engineer to CIO
  • Clearly articulate the Alkira value proposition, with a good understanding of the market, industry and competitive landscape
  • Partner with Alkira Account Managers to understand customer requirements and pain points. Assist with any technical asks from customers and help respond to RFP/RFIs
  • Scope, run and win Proof of Concepts end to end, with senior SE support on the largest and most complex engagements
  • Assist customers with design and deployment based on best practices
  • Work with the Alkira Product Management team to provide feedback on upcoming features from the customer's lens
  • Track and drive key customer features/asks with Alkira Product Management to implementation
  • Contribute to the wider SE team — we review each other's designs, share what works in the field, and build the reusable material the whole team sells with

What you need

  • 4+ years in a customer-facing pre-sales engineering role — Sales Engineer, Systems Engineer, Solutions Consultant or Solutions Architect — ideally at a networking or security vendor, cloud provider, channel partner, or consultancy.
  • Strong networking fundamentals – Everything below builds on this, and it is not negotiable
  • Good working knowledge of routing protocols and technologies, including BGP, OSPF, and static routing, with hands-on experience in route policy design, route redistribution, and filtering
  • Good understanding of network virtualization and software-defined networking, including VRFs, multi-tenant network architectures, SD-WAN, and the encapsulation protocols used to build overlays (GRE, VXLAN, and similar)
  • Hands-on experience with IPsec VPNs, encryption standards, NAT, and secure connectivity architectures
  • Good understanding of how enterprises extend cloud connectivity using a variety of networking technologies (e.g., Cloud On-Ramps, SD-WAN and IPsec)
  • Experience contributing to enterprise network design and deployment across data center, WAN or hybrid/multi-cloud environments
  • Good understanding of network services — DNS, DHCP, load balancing, traffic inspection and similar
  • The ability to troubleshoot in front of a customer across routing, security and cloud domains, with the wider SE team behind you on the hardest problems
  • Excellent written and verbal communication, and comfort presenting and demoing to customers in person – In this role you are the technical credibility of the company

Strongly preferred

  • Understanding of cloud networking constructs across AWS, Azure, and GCP (e.g., VPCs/VNets, Transit Gateway, Virtual WAN, Cloud Router, peering, and hybrid connectivity such as Direct Connect and ExpressRoute)
  • Network security experience, including firewalls (e.g., Palo Alto Networks, Fortinet, Check Point), firewall policy design, service insertion/chaining, and Zero Trust principles
  • Relevant technical certifications (e.g., CCNA/CCNP, AWS Advanced Networking, Azure Network Engineer, PCNSE)

  • BA/BS/MS in a technical field
  • Strong passion for sales and creating long-lasting professional relationships

Founded by Amir and Atif Khan, the creators of Viptela and pioneers of the SD-WAN market, Alkira was built to radically simplify how enterprises deploy and manage network infrastructure. Today, as part of Lumen, we are bringing that cloud-native operating model to a global network foundation trusted by the world's largest enterprises.

Our platform helps customers move faster without managing hardware, stitching together providers, or operating fragmented cloud networks. At Alkira, you'll help shape the next chapter of networking: cloud-like consumption, private-network performance, and total control across the enterprise. We move fast, solve hard problems, and build technology that changes how global businesses connect.

Join us and help build the future of networking.

Description

Upwind is a next-generation Cloud Security Platform that leverages runtime context to identify and prioritize critical risks, providing precise insights and efficient cloud security management. Unlike traditional tools, Upwind uses runtime data proactively for risk prioritization and posture insights, ensuring teams focus on what truly matters. With industry-leading efficiency and eBPF-powered sensors, Upwind delivers comprehensive capabilities, including agentless cloud posture discovery, real-time threat protection, and integrated API security. From misconfigurations to malware defense, Upwind ensures end-to-end, cost-effective cloud infrastructure protection. At Upwind, you’ll have the opportunity to think creatively, explore new ideas, and use your skills to make a meaningful impact on our growth.

We are looking for a Security Engineer to join our MDR team as the founding U.S. member of the Security organization. In this role, you will be part of our security function, focusing on proactive reviews and providing advanced guidance to customers, while independently owning U.S.-hours coverage. This is an opportunity to bring deep cloud security expertise to a fast-growing team, working closely with analysts, researchers, and engineers — with a clear path toward technical or team leadership as the U.S. presence scales.

Responsibilities

  • Assist in fine-tuning Upwind's detection and response mechanisms.
  • Support proactive reviews of customer environments to identify risks, exposed attack surfaces, and recommend improvements.
  • Lead and conduct in-depth security investigations — including supply chain, API, malware, and runtime attack scenarios — documenting outcomes and developing playbooks to enhance future detection and response.
  • Collaborate with Security Analysts, Research, and Backend teams to enhance detection quality.
  • Own the handling of complex or critical incidents escalated from Tier 1/2, including live, high-pressure engagements with customers.
  • Participate in recurring customer meetings, helping translate security findings into clear, actionable recommendations — and maintain composure when conversations get tense.
  • Stay up to date with emerging threats, attack techniques, attack surfaces, and best practices in cloud security.
  • Contribute to the development and training of AI-driven detection models, leveraging machine learning to improve investigation accuracy and response efficiency.

Requirements

  • Visa sponsorship is not available.
  • This role includes participating in a shared on-call rotation. While escalations are infrequent, team members are expected to be available for nights, weekends, or holidays during their rotation week.
  • Solid, hands-on experience in cybersecurity, ideally from a leading cloud or cloud security company, with real-world exposure to cloud environments.
  • Strong working knowledge of detection engineering, incident response, and threat analysis, with the ability to explain attack techniques (supply chain, API, malware, runtime) in depth.
  • Hands-on experience with at least one major cloud platform (AWS, GCP, or Azure) and container technologies (Docker/Kubernetes).
  • Comfortable and hands-on with Linux; Windows knowledge is a plus.
  • Familiarity with networking fundamentals and scripting (Python/Bash).
  • Strong communication and presentation skills, with proven ability to engage directly with customers — including staying composed under pressure or pushback.
  • Self-directed and comfortable operating independently in a fast-paced, high-ownership startup environment.
  • Curiosity, problem-solving mindset, and a genuine personal interest in security beyond the day job.
  • B.Sc. in Computer Science / Information Security — an advantage.

In this role, you will own the day-to-day execution of revenue accounting as AcuityMD scales. You will make sure revenue is recognized accurately, on time, and in line with ASC 606 across subscription, usage-based, and professional services contracts. You will partner with Sales, RevOps, Legal, and Finance so complex deals are understood before they close, and you will help build the controls and processes that keep us audit-ready as we grow.

Responsibilities

  • Revenue recognition: Apply ASC 606 to new and amended contracts, including performance obligations, standalone selling price allocation, contract modifications, and variable consideration for usage-based fees.
  • Month-end and quarter-end close: Prepare revenue entries, deferred revenue schedules, and contract-level reconciliations on a predictable close calendar.
  • Systems and data integrity: Maintain the sub-ledger flow between HubSpot and Rillet, reconcile contract data to revenue schedules, and flag gaps before they reach the close.
  • Contract review and deal support: Review non-standard terms such as discounts, free or bundled services, and renewals and upsells, and give Sales and Deal Desk fast, clear guidance on revenue treatment.
  • Commissions accounting: Support capitalized contract cost accounting under ASC 340-40, including amortization schedules and period-end true-ups. [Confirm scope with Jess]
  • Audit readiness: Build and maintain support for revenue and deferred revenue balances, draft technical memos, and respond to auditor requests.
  • Process improvement: Document procedures, tighten controls, and automate manual steps so the function scales without adding headcount at the same pace.
  • Cross-functional partnership: Explain revenue implications in plain language to non-finance teams and help reduce close-time fire drills.

Your Profile

  • Bachelor's degree in Accounting or Finance; CPA or CPA-eligible preferred.
  • 4–6 years of revenue accounting experience in public accounting and/or a high-growth SaaS company.
  • Hands-on ASC 606 experience with multi-element and usage-based contracts, including SSP analysis and contract modifications.
  • Experience owning a revenue close, including deferred revenue roll-forwards and reconciliations.
  • Comfort with cloud ERP and billing systems (Rillet experience a plus) and strong Excel or Google Sheets skills.
  • Clear communicator who can explain GAAP to Sales, Legal, and executive stakeholders.
  • Detail-oriented and proactive, with a bias toward improving the process, not only running it.

Nice to Haves

  • B2B SaaS experience, ideally MedTech or another regulated vertical.
  • Usage-based or hybrid pricing experience and the related ASC 606 implications.
  • Experience with ASC 340-40 deferred commissions.
  • Familiarity with HubSpot CRM and its integration to a revenue sub-ledger.
  • Exposure to SOX scoping or public company readiness work.

AcuityMD is committed to providing highly competitive cash compensation, equity, and benefits. The compensation offered for this role will be based on multiple factors such as location, the role's scope and complexity, and the candidate's experience and expertise, market data and may vary from the range provided. Base salary range: $100,000-$130,000

You must have an eligible work permit in the USA to be considered for this position.

We Offer:

  • Ground floor opportunity: Join a high-growth startup, backed by world-class investors across Enterprise SaaS and Medical Devices (Benchmark, Redpoint Ventures, and Ajax Health).
  • Learning Budget: Reimbursements for relevant learning and up-skilling opportunities.
  • Remote work: AcuityMD is committed to supporting full-remote flexibility for employees in the US. We provide a work-from-home stipend for all employees.
  • Flexible PTO: Generous time off and flexible hours give you the freedom to do your best work.
  • Paid Health, Dental, and Vision Plans: We offer 100% paid health, dental, and vision plans for all employees and 75% paid for our employees' dependents.
  • Home Office Stipend: $1,000 to invest in remote office equipment and WiFi reimbursement.
  • Optional Team Retreats: We meet in-person multiple times per year for co-working and social gatherings.

Who We Are:

The Company: We are builders, who are inspired by our mission to expand patient access to cutting-edge medical technologies. We value working collaboratively to solve hard problems for our customers with simple, innovative solutions. We push ourselves to learn with empathy. We foster an active culture of mentorship and inclusion, and we welcome new team members that share our values.

We're backed by Benchmark, Redpoint Ventures, Ajax Health, ICONIQ Growth and several other leading software and medical device investors. Since Acuity launched in 2020, we've brought on customers ranging from publicly traded Fortune 500 companies to innovative growth-stage companies and regional medical device distributors.

The Product: AcuityMD uses data and software to help teams collaborate around the complex relationships they have with the users of medical technologies: doctors. Our platform empowers medical technology companies to see how their products are used, understand why outcomes vary, and identify opportunities where physicians or sites of care can better serve their patients.

AcuityMD is a remote-first company. We believe the best talent isn't confined to one zip code, so our team works from wherever they do their best work, across the U.S.

We also believe some of our best work happens face-to-face. Critical projects move faster, our products get better, and our community gets stronger when we're in the same room, so we bring the team together throughout the year for company-wide and team on-sites built around that work.

In practice: expect 4-5 in-person opportunities a year through company/team on-sites and in-person collaboration for critical projects. If you're based near our Boston hub, there's no set requirement for how often you come into the office, that's your call, based on what works best for you and your team.

We do not discriminate on the basis of race, gender, religion, color, national origin, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status. Extend is revolutionizing the post-purchase experience for retailers and their customers by providing merchants with AI-driven solutions that enhance customer satisfaction and drive revenue growth. Today, Extend works with more than 1,000 leading merchant partners across industries, including fashion/apparel, cosmetics, furniture, jewelry, consumer electronics, auto parts, sports and fitness, and much more. Extend is backed by some of the most prominent technology investors in the industry, and our headquarters is in downtown San Francisco.

About the Role:

The Director of Compliance will provide strategic leadership over Extend's regulatory compliance function, setting the direction and long-term roadmap for the infrastructure that underpins Extend's service contract and insurance programs across North America, including all licensing. Reporting directly to Extend's VP, Deputy General Counsel, this person will serve as a trusted advisor and subject matter expert to the executive team on regulatory strategy, risk, and governance, representing compliance in front of regulators, auditors, and cross-functional leadership. This is a strategy and leadership role: you'll set the vision for how compliance scales with the business, build out the team and its structure, and be the executive-level voice for compliance across the company.

What You'll Be Doing:

  • Set the strategic direction and long-term roadmap for Extend's regulatory compliance program, spanning licensing, service contract terms and conditions, and insurance partner relationships, ensuring the function scales with the business.
  • Serve as the executive-level owner for regulatory and licensing matters across both business-as-usual operations and new products or initiatives, providing judgment and direction where complexity or risk requires it.
  • Partner with the rest of the compliance team to set priorities, unblock cross-functional dependencies, and continuously improve how terms and conditions, license applications, filings, approvals, and renewals get done.
  • Represent Extend in significant regulatory examinations, inquiries, and audits, working alongside the compliance team and outside counsel.
  • Monitor the regulatory landscape, proactively advising leadership on emerging requirements and risk.
  • Coach and develop the compliance team, and help define the function's long-term structure and career paths as Extend scales.
  • Partner with cross-functional teams to embed compliance requirements into merchant onboarding, customer experience, contracting, product workflows and program design.
  • Provide active guidance to leadership on how compliance strategy supports business goals, balancing rigor with the speed the business needs.
  • Establish and monitor KPIs for licensing accuracy, timeliness, and cost, and drive continuous improvement across processes and vendor relationships.
  • Set direction on service contract terms and conditions in partnership with outside counsel, reviewing for regulatory accuracy and completeness.

  • Proven, action- and solution-oriented compliance leader with the ability to operate effectively in both strategic and hands-on environments.

jobs.description:
MOFGA Certification Services, LLC (MCS) is hiring a full time Organic Certification Specialist (Livestock/Dairy focused) to join our team. MCS is a USDA-accredited organic certifier, certifying over 500 crop, livestock, and handling operations in Maine, New Hampshire, and Massachusetts. The Certification Specialist provides high quality customer service along with skilled review and auditing verification to support positive organic certification experiences for organic producers in our service territory, while upholding the USDA National Organic Program regulations. The ideal candidate will have education and experience in organic regulations, organic and/or sustainable farming methods and production, and familiarity with the various production scopes that MCS certifies. Experience in food processing is a plus. The Certification Specialist reports to the MCS Director and works collaboratively with MCS staff, specialists, and inspectors. This position requires some field work, including inspections, residue sampling, and investigations. Priority will be given to candidates who apply before November 13, 2026

Overview: The Certification Specialist provides high quality customer service along with skilled review and auditing verification to support positive organic certification experiences for organic producers in our service territory, while upholding the USDA National Organic Program regulations. This position assesses compliance of an operation’s organic system plan, reviews inspection reports, and issues subsequent responses, primarily within the livestock and dairy scopes. This position works collaboratively with other certification specialists, inspection program manager, and inspectors, and conducts inspections and pesticide residue sampling as time allows. Certification Specialists also support the MCS quality management system, and may represent MCS at conferences or other MOFGA events. Contributing to MCS policy development, writing pieces for MCS’ newsletter, The Organic Sprout, is an expectation for this position.

Supervisor: Director of MOFGA Certification Services

Position: Salaried. Federal Fair Labor Standards Act exempt. The employee is not eligible for overtime payment. This position is part of the MOFGA Workers United Union bargaining unit.

Work Week: 40 hours - Monday through Friday. Additional evening and weekend hours as required.

Salary Range: This is a salaried position, with a starting salary range of $50,000-$55,000 annually, dependent upon experience. MOFGA has an excellent benefits package, including paid medical, dental and vision insurance, and parental leave. Employees receive a generous paid time off package, including vacation and sick time, three personal days, two week-long office closures, 14 paid holidays annually, and a sabbatical after seven years of employment.

Location: This position is remote, requiring travel within MCS’ service territory, and off-site visits to client’s farms and production facilities. The service territory includes the state of Maine, the state of New Hampshire, and the northeastern areas of Massachusetts. Our offices are located in Unity, Maine and staff are welcome to work from this office as much as they like. Will need to travel to Unity for occasional meetings and required participation in the Common Ground Country Fair. This position is required to be based within the MCS service territory.

Requirements:

  • Education or experience in organic certification or regulatory compliance, including inspections and auditing.
  • Knowledge of the USDA-National Organic Program standards, especially as it applies to crop, livestock/dairy, , and processing.
  • Working knowledge of organic or sustainable crop and livestock farms, dairies, and food processing.
  • A demonstrated ability to communicate effectively, especially in writing.
  • Excellent organizational skills
  • Proficiency in computer software, including databases and collaborative platforms.
  • Strong interpersonal skills that welcome collaboration and constructive feedback.
  • Valid driver’s license and reliable vehicle
  • A commitment to MOFGA’s mission and values.
  • IOIA training and prior organic inspection experience a plus
  • College degree in agriculture or related field a plus
  • Must be able to travel to attend meetings, training workshops and conferences.
  • Participate in MOFGA’s Common Ground Country Fair as needed.

Certification Specialist Responsibilities:

  • Performs certification activities for clients including these specific activities:
    • Perform technical reviews of organic system plans, primarily within the livestock and dairy scope. Communicates according to policy with producers about the results of these reviews.
    • Review inspection reports for these same clients. Communicates according to policy with producers about the results of these reviews.
    • Assists applicants by explaining the organic standards and the certification process, encouraging them to take advantage of the technical services offered by MOFGA.
    • Pursues adverse actions with clients in accordance with MCS policy and in coordination with colleagues/supervisors.
    • Keeps track of clients; assures that auditable files are in good order.
  • Conduct annual, investigative and/or unannounced inspections or residue sampling as time allows.
  • Performs material review of products as needed and in conjunction with other MCS staff and agency affiliates.
  • Investigates complaints to protect the integrity of the organic label. Pursues adverse actions, as necessary.
  • Participation in MCS internal audits and NOP accreditation audits.
  • Other duties and responsibilities as deemed necessary to carry out MOFGA’s certification program and maintain accreditation with USDA.

Physical Requirements: Ability to walk long distances over rough terrain; occasional light lifting; ability to drive and travel long distances by car. Able to work in outdoor conditions that include all types of seasonal weather, as well as, inside environments where there may be loud noises or strong odors. Ability to sit for long periods to complete computer-based work, participate in meetings, and conduct organic inspections, whether in person or over video conference platforms.

The Maine Organic Farmers and Gardeners Association (MOFGA) is a broad-based community that supports farmers, empowers people to feed their communities, and advocates for an organic future. Our vision is a future where local organic farming nourishes all people, and sustains thriving ecosystems, healthy communities, and fair economies. jobs.excerpt: WHO ARE WE? Launch Potato is the discovery and conversion company.
jobs.description:
WHO ARE WE?

Launch Potato is the discovery and conversion company. We reach tens of millions of people every month through our brands, including FinanceBuzz, All About Cookies, and OnlyInYourState. We turn that attention into real outcomes for our partners, some of the world's leading companies.

Our mission: create predictable, high-value customer acquisition at scale by connecting discovery, intent, and performance across category-leading consumer brands in finance, travel, and entertainment.

We run profitable and bootstrapped, with a South Florida HQ and a remote-first team across 18 countries.

WHY JOIN US?

You own outcomes here, not tasks. We measure work by impact, not activity. The pace is real, and change is constant, so the people who do best turn change into opportunity instead of waiting for it to settle. Feedback runs direct and lands with respect. Ordinary people make themselves extraordinary at Launch Potato.

YOUR ROLE

You'll build the models that decide which carrier each auto insurance shopper sees on our click wall. The goal is to send every user to the carrier most likely to convert them, so carriers see our traffic convert and raise their bids. You'll also own the buying models behind our media spend, which are held to ROAS.

Carrier conversion data (quotes, policies and acquisition cost) is now coming back to us, and you'll be the one who puts it to work in production. The hard part is the data. Outcomes land weeks or months after the click, many sessions are sparse, the same shoppers come back, and the market drifts. Our bids also decide which users we win, so the model shapes the data it learns from next.

This is a hands-on individual contributor role. You frame problems directly with the business, find your own data, build and validate the model, and stay with it through deployment and monitoring. An ML engineer works alongside you on the production side. Auto insurance takes most of your time to start, and scope broadens to other verticals over time.

We're remote first, and most of the company works East Coast hours.

WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

By day 60, you run our insurance marketplace media buying on your own.

By the end of your first year:

  • Click wall serving that matches each user to the right carrier
  • Carrier conversion data running in production models
  • Automated marketplace bidding taken from proof of concept to scale
  • A clear approach for repeat users and sparse sessions
  • Production models that hold up through drift and changing objectives
  • Output the business trusts and uses without rework

MUST HAVE

  • 5+ years of hands-on applied data science with measurable business impact
  • Your models drove paid media decisions: spend, bidding or ad serving. Attribution and reporting alone don't qualify.
  • You built what's on your resume and can explain it down to the loss function and architecture choice, neural network fundamentals included
  • You see how today's bids shape tomorrow's training data, and you've handled late labels, sparse features or drift
  • You own models end to end: you find your own data, build through deployment and monitoring, and bring a point of view
  • Expert Python and SQL

NICE TO HAVES

  • Real ad budget spent in live auctions
  • Large-scale ranking or recommendation systems
  • Explaining tradeoffs to non-technical partners in plain terms
  • Designing for auction feedback loops, selection bias and exploration
  • Hands-on neural network work, such as embeddings of text, creative or user behavior
  • AWS for data science: ECS, S3, Athena, SageMaker
  • CI/CD deployment

Want to accelerate your career? Apply now!

About The Role

We are looking for a Staff Salesforce Engineer for the Product & Technology (P&T) team at The RealReal. We want someone who will push our engineering standards forward, solve the hard problems, and lead our charge into AI-driven automation.You’ll be the main technical point person for our marketing tools (specifically Zoom, Sumo, and LeanData) and will play a critical role in our Q2 AI initiatives. What You Get To Do Every Day

This includes staying hands-on with the codebase, developing applications using Apex Classes, Triggers, Lightning Web Components (LWC), VisualForce Pages, and Aura Components.

jobs.description:
The Senior Manager, Customer Success and Renewals is a business, sales and solutions thought leader at CDW, responsible for the development and execution of the business unit’s future vision across both the Customer Success and Renewals disciplines. Partnering with sales and solutions and utilizing actionable analytics, this role ensures that Customer Success Managers, Renewal Managers, and supporting roles are delivering to customer outcomes and to retention, renewal, and growth targets. This leader owns the strategies that underpin both functions – the Customer Success lifecycle strategy (Land, Adopt, Expand, Retain) and the renewals strategy that converts adoption into on-time, full-value retention and expansion – and ensures the two operate as one connected motion rather than two hand-offs. The Senior Manager demonstrates focus in leading Managers and Coworkers to achieve financial, operational, and strategic goals, balancing business financials and operational results while maintaining a strong coworker and customer focus. The Senior Manager is a visionary with an objective and pulse on next level customer support, drives strategy, forecasts and evolves the vision of Customer Success and Renewals, understands best in class practices, and inspires innovation. This role is expected to be proficient in the application of AI within the execution of the role, and to define and drive an AI strategy within the team that delivers on the digital strategies required to execute the business unit’s strategy.

What You Will Do

  • Design and drive the business unit’s future vision and strategy across Customer Success and Renewals, aligning the Customer Success methodologies (Land, Adopt, Expand, Retain) and renewals lifecycle (Forecast, Quote, Negotiate, Close, Retain) to ensure both functions operate as one connected motion and are aligned to individual, team, organization, and company goals.
  • Own the renewals strategy for the business unit – forecast accuracy, on-time renewal rate, retention and churn mitigation, multi-year commitments, and expansion – and align it to the adoption strategy so that customer outcomes evidenced through Customer Success drive renewal results.
  • Own the financial management and performance of the Customer Success and Renewals team by defining and managing analytical KPIs across adoption, customer health, renewal rate, on-time renewal, retention, churn, forecast accuracy, and expansion, and deliver against quarterly and long-term financial, operational, and strategic targets.
  • Execute the AI and digital strategy within the Customer Success and Renewals team by prioritizing and adopting relevant use cases, enabling teams to effectively leverage AI and digital capabilities, measuring impact, and ensuring responsible and compliant use.
  • Champion the effective use of the underlying data and digital foundation—including customer health, telemetry, entitlement, and renewal data—to support AI-enabled and digital-led engagement and scale coverage across the team.
  • Be proficient in the use of AI within the execution of the role, applying enterprise AI-enabled tools and insights—such as Copilot, Cowork, and Section Coach—to customer health scoring, renewal forecasting, risk identification, account planning, coworker productivity, and other applicable business needs.
  • Attract, retain, coach, and develop talent by providing meaningful performance feedback, creating individual development plans, and fostering a culture that supports the growth and advancement of internal talent to execute the business unit’s integrated Customer Success and Renewals strategy.
  • Serve as the subject matter expert on Customer Success, Renewals, relevant business unit trends, and industry practices, using these insights to evolve the Customer Success and Renewals strategy and drive improved customer outcomes and retention.
  • Develop and execute customer segmentation strategies for the business unit, aligning team resources and engagement models to customer needs, value, and growth opportunities.
  • Partner with sales, OEM and partner organizations, and finance on renewal pricing, quoting, and negotiation strategies that protect margin while demonstrating value to the customer.
  • Enforce best practices, motivate, and influence through a culture of Continuous Quality Improvement.
  • Be an example of our values, The CDW Way, and enforce coworkers to build rapport and corporative relationships with customers and peers while meeting their expectations.


What We Expect of You

Minimum basic requirements

  • Bachelor’s degree in Business Management or a related field, or equivalent experience.
  • 10+ years of experience in Technology Services or Solutions, with demonstrated expertise in Customer Success, Renewals, Retention, or related customer lifecycle functions.
  • 3+ years of experience building, leading, and managing teams focused on Customer Success, Renewals, or both, including experience leading or partnering closely with renewals, retention, subscription, or contract management functions.
  • Strong understanding of the customer and subscription lifecycle, including customer health and adoption, renewal forecasting, retention and churn metrics, expansion, and contract management practices.
  • Strong financial and business acumen, with the ability to analyze performance, manage financial and operational KPIs, and translate insights into strategies that drive retention, growth, and profitability.
  • Thorough knowledge of operational strategies and enterprise infrastructure, with the ability to translate business and customer needs into strategies that drive customer outcomes, retention, and business performance.
  • Demonstrated proficiency with AI tools in a professional setting, including applying AI to daily workflows and coaching teams on effective, responsible, and compliant use.
  • Excellent executive-level interpersonal, written, presentation, consulting, and influencing skills, with the ability to effectively navigate complex or difficult situations, build alignment, and influence customer and internal stakeholders.
  • Demonstrated ability to lead through complexity, manage high-stress workloads, assess and mitigate risks, coordinate cross-functional initiatives, and develop high-performing teams.
  • Ability to travel up to 50%.

Preferred skills, experience and qualities needed

  • Experience with advanced technology solutions and emerging technologies, particularly within a technology services or solutions environment.
  • Applicable Customer Success Management certification(s).
  • Experience defining and deploying an AI or digital adoption strategy within a customer-facing organization.

Annual bonus target of 25% subject to terms and conditions of plan

CDW is committed to being an AI-fluent organization

As a leader, you will champion and be accountable for our vision of becoming an AI-fluent organization.   4. Leads approved improvements to claim-handling procedures, workflows, escalation practices, and technical training. Uses claim trends and operational findings to establish improvement priorities, implement changes, and assess resulting outcomes.

  13. jobs.excerpt: OverviewPowerLines is a national nonprofit organization that aims to modernize the utility regulatory system for American energy consumers to lower utility bills and grow the economy.
jobs.description:
Overview

PowerLines is a national nonprofit organization that aims to modernize the utility regulatory system for American energy consumers to lower utility bills and grow the economy. It focuses on state public utilities commissions (PUCs), which play a critical role in determining how much people pay for utility bills, how utilities invest in different types of energy, and where new energy projects are built. These 200 commissioners oversee more than $200 billion in utility spending each year and have significant influence over the future of our energy system.

Utility affordability is quickly becoming one of the most pressing economic challenges facing American consumers. In 2025, utilities requested a record-setting $31 billion in rate increases, double the previous record, while 80 million Americans are struggling to pay their utility bills. Meanwhile, the U.S. grid is experiencing the fastest rise in electricity demand in decades with the growth of AI data centers and manufacturing, and utilities plan to spend $1.4 trillion by 2030. Policymakers across the political spectrum are increasingly focused on how regulatory systems can respond to these pressures while protecting consumers and supporting economic growth.

Recognized on the 2025 “TIME100 Next” list, PowerLines is rapidly becoming a go-to source and leader in informing the national discussion of this issue and has already shaped the conversation in the New York Times, Washington Post, Wall Street Journal, Politico, Bloomberg, CBS News, NPR, Marketplace, Financial Times, TIME, Vox, The Daily Mail, and MIT Technology Review. PowerLines is quickly establishing credibility as a nonpartisan expert on utility regulatory and energy affordability issues while reaching a bipartisan set of policymakers, including initial partnerships with the National Governors Association, Western Governors Association, and National Conference of State Legislatures.

PowerLines is in a period of significant organizational growth and seeks a full-time Head of Policy to build and lead the organization’s Policy Team. This is a senior, hands-on role, and having strong leadership skills is a must. The Head of Policy will lead development and execution of PowerLines’ policy strategy, including engagement with policymakers, particularly at the state level such as governors, state legislators, and state energy offices, and on policy opportunities more broadly. (Note: The Policy Team engages at both the state and federal policy levels, but focuses on state-level policymaking engagement.) The Head of Policy will wear many different hats, from leading a growing team of policy experts while building partnerships and coalitions to advising stakeholders on policy strategy issues and serving as an external spokesperson for PowerLines. This is a rare opportunity for an experienced leader to shape how the utility regulatory system responds to rising utility bills and surging electricity demand, at an organization with the visibility and relationships to influence outcomes nationally.

The Head of Policy will be one of PowerLines’ senior programmatic leaders and serve on the PowerLines executive leadership team. The Head of Policy works alongside the Regulatory Team and Communications Team to drive impact in policymaking venues.

PowerLines is headquartered in Washington, DC. The Head of Policy is a remote position, with travel of approximately 10 to 20 percent expected. The Head of Policy will report directly to the Founder and Executive Director.

(Note: PowerLines is currently also recruiting for a Head of Regulatory role. The Head of Regulatory role is intended to be more technical on utility regulatory issues, whereas the Head of Policy role is intended to be more policy generalist in nature.)

Requirements

Key Responsibilities

  • Team Leadership
    • Oversee Policy Team currently consisting of a full-time State Policy Lead, part-time Policy Advisors, and part-time Senior Advisors
    • Lead Policy Team meetings on a weekly basis and set team priorities, manage workflow and workstreams across team, and ensure quality control on all policy products
    • Serve on PowerLines’ executive leadership team and provide counsel on policy issues, opportunities, developments, and strategy
    • Own day-to-day policy and team management decisions, and bring decisions on programmatic strategy, flagship products, highest-stakes external relationships, budget, senior hiring, and final personnel actions to the leadership team
    • Provide mentorship to junior team members on programmatic and organizational issues
    • Lead hiring for the Policy Team as it grows, in partnership with the Chief of Staff, who owns the recruitment and hiring process, with the Executive Director making final decisions on senior hires
    • Define scopes for and direct the work of Senior Advisors and policy consultants
  • Policy Campaign Strategy and Execution
    • Develop PowerLines’ annual policy strategy to be updated on a regular basis, including identification of team goals, OKRs, and internal calendar with key dates and timelines, with the Executive Director
    • Develop campaign strategy for 2027 policy campaigns across states, including recommending priority states and engagement strategy in each state
    • Execute policy engagement strategy with policymakers, particularly at the state level including governors, state legislators, and state energy offices, including partnership and coalition building, policymaker education, and technical assistance
    • Vet and recommend consultants and lobbyists as needed, with final engagement and budget decisions made by the Executive Director
    • Oversee regular tracking and reporting of PowerLines' policy impact to iteratively inform strategy development and execution
    • Oversee compliance with lobbying registration and filing requirements
  • Policy Product Development, Research, and Analysis
    • Oversee development and distribution of key PowerLines policy products, including policy playbooks, dashboards, and issue briefs, with Executive Director sign-off on flagship products
    • Oversee the tracking and monitoring of key utility regulatory policy developments and legislation happening across the country
    • Lead drafting and preparation of written communications, testimony, and thought leadership as needed
  • Policymaker Education and Engagement
    • Serve as a key ambassador of PowerLines with policymakers including governors, state legislators, and state energy offices, coordinating with the Executive Director on the highest-stakes relationships
    • Lead relationship building with key policymaker network partners, including National Governors Association, Western Governors Association, Midwestern Governors Association, National Conference of State Legislatures, National Association of State Energy Officials, and other policymaker networks
    • Oversee provision of research and technical assistance to support policymakers
    • Oversee development and execution of “utility regulation 101” briefings for policymakers and partners less familiar with utility regulatory issues
  • Coalition Building and Stakeholder Engagement
    • Conduct landscape assessment of current and target coalition partners to engage on utility regulatory issues
    • Build partnerships with coalition partners reflecting PowerLines’ commitment to bipartisan, multi-sectoral, and cross-customer class engagement
    • Lead relationship building with key coalition partners, including managing existing coalitions and partners and building new ones
    • Coordinate with the Executive Director on engagement with senior policymakers and key partners
  • External Representation and Fundraising
    • Represent PowerLines on external engagement and speaking opportunities, including media inquiries, event speaking opportunities, reporter and podcast interviews, committee hearings, workshops, and roundtables, in coordination with the Executive Director and Communications Team
    • Support Strategy & Operations Team in developing donor communications, grant, and other fundraising materials
    • Regularly update and maintain an internal tracker of major policy accomplishments and successes to inform PowerLines’ policy impact
    • Attend relevant events and conferences (e.g., NGA, NCSL)
  • Cross-Team Coordination
    • Coordinate with Regulatory Team and Communications Team on issues and workstreams impacting multiple teams
    • Coordinate with Communications Team to equip reporters and other media partners with key 101-level materials relevant to policy work
    • Coordinate with Communications Team on policy content in communications products
    • Partner with the Chief of Staff, who owns cross-team prioritization and capacity allocation, to plan Regulatory and Communications Team support for policy priorities

Qualifications

Required Qualifications:

  • 10+ years of experience in state or federal policy, legislative affairs, or advocacy
  • Experience managing, mentoring, and developing staff, including strong leadership skills and emotional intelligence
  • Proven record of developing and executing multi-state legislative or policy campaigns that delivered results
  • Strong relationships with governors’ offices, state legislators, and policymaker networks such as NGA and NCSL
  • Experience working across the political spectrum and keeping positions nonpartisan in a politically sensitive issue area
  • Experience building and managing coalitions with diverse partners
  • Comfort building systems and processes in a startup environment
  • Excellent writer and communicator who can turn complex policy into clear products for policymakers and represent an organization in a diverse range of settings
  • Comfort operating as both a senior strategic leader and a hands-on individual contributor on a small team in a rapidly growing organization

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Deep knowledge of energy, utility, or consumer protection policy, including how legislation interacts with utility regulation
  • Established relationships with consumer advocates, public utilities commissions, and regulatory networks
  • Experience working in or with state government, such as governor’s office, state legislator’s office, or other similar venues is a plus
  • Experience supporting grant proposals and funder reporting
  • Experience scoping and managing consultants, lobbyists, and budgets

Benefits

Compensation and Benefits

  • The expected salary range for this role is $175,000-$225,000. Compensation may be based on skills, qualifications, experience, location, and other factors.
  • The benefits package includes unlimited PTO, paid holidays, health insurance, a 401k employer match, sick leave, and health and wellness benefits.

jobs.description:
About REPLUG

REPLUG is a Mobile Revenue Growth partner that helps companies turn mobile into a measurable driver of revenue, customer value and long-term business growth.

We connect acquisition, retention, measurement and app experience into a unified growth system that improves commercial performance. From global app publishers to established brands looking to unlock more value from mobile, we partner with companies that want to grow more efficiently and build sustainable growth.

Our work combines strategic thinking with hands-on execution across App Store Optimization, Paid User Acquisition, CRM, measurement and mobile growth consulting.

We are looking for a Demand Generation & Marketing Manager to build and run a marketing function that makes a measurable contribution to REPLUG’s commercial growth. Your primary objective is to generate qualified demand and sales opportunities from the businesses we want to work with, with a particular focus on higher-value engagements.

You’ll own the marketing plan, its execution and its performance. Working closely with the founders and Sales, you’ll decide where marketing should focus, challenge assumptions and connect marketing activity to qualified conversations, opportunities and pipeline value.

This is a hands-on role with broad ownership. You’ll combine commercial judgement with strong content and practical CRM skills, while ensuring our positioning and the experience prospects have with REPLUG remain consistent.

Success will be measured primarily through qualified opportunities generated, the quality and value of pipeline created, and marketing’s contribution to commercial growth.

What You’ll Do

Generate Demand from the Right Businesses

  • Plan and execute B2B campaigns around the problems, buying triggers and decision-makers within our priority customer profiles.

  • Choose and test the right mix of channels, including LinkedIn, email, partnerships, webinars and events, with a clear route from engagement to conversation.

  • Build campaign assets, landing pages and follow-up journeys. Work with Sales to improve targeting and lead quality using feedback from real conversations.

Own the Marketing Plan and Delivery

  • Translate business objectives into a clear marketing plan with priorities, campaigns, timelines, budgets and measures of success.

  • Make decisions about where to invest time and resources, explain your reasoning and challenge activities that lack a clear purpose.

  • Deliver core marketing activities yourself and coordinate contributions from founders, specialists and external partners. Keep delivery moving and identify where additional support is needed.

Own Content and Distribution

  • Coordinate founder and team LinkedIn activity, turning specialist insights and client results into relevant content for prospective buyers.

  • Create and commission case studies, website content and campaign materials. Own briefs, editorial quality, distribution and reuse across channels.

  • Develop partner activity that extends our reach into the right audiences. Keep messaging, tone and the prospect experience consistent across touchpoints.

Own CRM and Lead Nurturing

  • Own HubSpot marketing processes, including segmentation, forms, workflows, email nurturing, campaign tracking and data quality.

  • Build nurture journeys for contacts at different stages of interest, including those who fit our target profile but are not ready to buy.

  • Agree qualification criteria and handover processes with Sales. Make sure relevant leads reach the right person with useful context and clear next steps.

Understand Performance and Improve It

  • Track how marketing contributes to qualified conversations and pipeline. Report marketing-sourced and marketing-influenced opportunities separately.

  • Review conversion between stages with Sales, identify where prospects drop out and adjust campaigns, messaging or nurturing accordingly.

  • Use results to decide what to continue, change or stop. Explain what is working, what remains uncertain and what you will test next.

What We’re Looking For

We care about demonstrated impact and your personal contribution. You should be able to explain a campaign you owned, the decisions you made, and the commercial opportunities it generated.

  • 3 to 5 years of proven, hands-on B2B marketing experience, including campaigns designed to generate qualified demand for services or products through a considered sales process.

  • Commercial awareness and a clear understanding of customer fit, lead qualification, sales cycles and pipeline progression.

  • Strong content judgement and excellent written and spoken English. You can turn specialist knowledge into clear, credible messaging for buyers.

  • Practical HubSpot experience, including segmentation, workflows, nurturing and reporting. You can build and improve the setup yourself.

  • Experience owning a marketing plan and delivering it within limited resources, while coordinating colleagues and external contributors.

  • The confidence to challenge the founders constructively, make recommendations and take responsibility for the outcome.

  • Good brand judgement and the ability to balance immediate demand generation with long-term credibility.

Nice to Have

  • Experience marketing an agency, consultancy or other B2B services business.

  • Familiarity with mobile marketing, AdTech or the app growth ecosystem.

  • Experience building demand through founder visibility, expert content, partnerships or industry events.

  • Based in a location with convenient flight connections to Berlin, Germany.

What We Offer

  • Ownership of REPLUG’s marketing plan, with senior marketing guidance, direct access to the founders and influence over priorities.

  • Access to REPLUG’s specialists, client results and industry relationships. You’ll lead and coordinate delivery, with specialist support so you can focus your hands-on work where it has the greatest impact.

  • The opportunity to shape how REPLUG reaches its next clients and demonstrate a clear contribution to business growth.

  • A fully remote setup, with travel opportunities to attend industry and REPLUG’s events

  • A EUR 1,000 annual educational budget

If you are looking for a new opportunity to grow with a clinician founded and clinician led organization, look no further! Hospitals, community clinics, investment bank funded group practice startups, state agencies, and more.

At OptiMindHealth, we continuously strive to provide consistent, high-quality care and expand the reach of mental health care services in our communities. Unfortunately, the need often outpaces the services available to those we serve and only adds to the current mental health crisis in our nation. To combat this crisis and further our mission, we need more compassionate and skilled clinicians to join our cause. We are not interested in the “burnt-out” clinician that no longer finds meaning in their work and is just going through the motions; we are seeking people with a passion to provide excellent care, and the belief that we, together, can make a difference. If that’s you, then you’re in the right place!

Our approach with our team is simple, we take care of you, the clinician, so you can take care of patients. How do we do that? By investing in your growth, supporting you financially, holistically, and professionally, while being flexible regarding your personal needs and goals. The work we do with patients is hard enough and over the years we have found that our team often does their best work when the administrative burdens are taken off their plate and they are able to be fully present with their patients. Our administrative support team handles all non-clinical tasks so that you don’t have to think about anything except focusing on your patients.

Why bother with the endless administrative burdens and isolation of private practice? Use your highly trained interpersonal skills to change the culture around mental health care, decrease stigma, and help people who need you, while being supported by an experienced multi-disciplinary team of clinicians. Let us take care of the rest!

Want to work part time? No problem. Want to do group therapy? Sure! Want to do long-term psychodynamic psychotherapy with all of your clients? We do it every day. Interested in treating couples? We can make that happen. Basically, what we are saying is that whatever outpatient care you are interested in providing, we can surely accommodate you. We know you have exceptional skills; we want you to be part of our team.

The perfect candidate will share our passion for improving and expanding access to high quality mental health care and will thrive in a culture that emphasizes creativity, authenticity, humor, compassion, acceptance, and determination. Telehealth or onsite, we support your authentic and unique growth trajectory, while being yourself and having some fun!

We prioritize the clinician's experience by offering excellent compensation, benefits, training/supervision, and flexibility. Whether you’re working from home or in one of our physical offices, if you’re doing it during your scheduled work hours, you’re getting paid for it. Our compensation packages include:

  • Starting Salary range: $62,000.00 - $80,000.00 per year.
  • 401K with maximum employee matching.
  • Health care benefits.
  • Generous paid vacation and sick leave time.
  • Paid administrative time for consultation, supervision, and documentation.
  • Full administrative support.

Here are a few extra perks our team loves:

  • Paid supervision, clinical rounds, and administrative time.
  • Customized schedules within available clinic hours.
  • Hybrid work environment if desired: Telehealth and/or in-person (in select locations).
  • Muti-disciplinary team approach to treatment.
  • Incredible administrative support team.
  • Company leadership that understands the practice of mental healthcare.
  • Inclusive, socially responsible, client focused leadership.
  • We are not a franchise or a big investor-backed company.
  • And most importantly, clinician-led and clinician-FOCUSED!

We know what it’s like to work in an organization led by businesspeople instead of clinicians. We, on the other hand, have organically grown as a socially responsible company that started as a single provider on a mission to destigmatize and broaden the reach of mental health care, to an integrated and holistic group of exceptional providers with diverse backgrounds working toward that mission. We are fortunate to have significantly increased the reach of mental health care services in our communities, and look forward to continuing to provide consistent, high-quality care to those we serve for many years to come.

We will rely on your expertise to:

  • Evaluate mental health conditions, diagnose, create, and implement a treatment plan, complete ongoing documentation including further diagnosis, treatment plan reviews, and case notes according to company policy.
  • Provide excellent care for clients and collaborate with a dynamic team to further the mission of filling gaps in our community.
  • Utilize creativity in interventions to help clients achieve and exceed goals.
  • Prepare and submit individual documentation for each session per company guidelines and protocol. 
  • For Full-Time status, clinicians must maintain at least 32 available hours for patient care per week.
  • Coordinate services with other care providers, families, work personnel, medical personnel, other OptiMindHealth staff, and school staff as needed.
  • Attend and participate in all clinical staff meetings and trainings.

Qualifications and Skill for This Positions: 

  • Master's degree in one of the behavioral sciences or related fields from an accredited college/university.
  • Full, current, unrestricted license to practice independently (LMHC, LCSW, LMFT) is required.

Additionally Valuable (but not essential) Qualifications for This Position: 

  • Experience working in community, group, or private practice mental health.

  • Specialty area of practice.

jobs.description:
About Aura Biosciences

Aura Biosciences is a clinical-stage biotechnology company developing bel-sar, a potentially transformative, first-in-class therapy for patients living with ocular cancers. Bel-sar represents an entirely novel approach to treating ocular cancers via its dual mechanisms of action of acute tumor necrosis and secondary anti-tumor immune activation. The Phase 3 registration study of Bel-sar in early choroidal melanoma, the largest patient segment of uveal melanoma, is fully enrolled, and earlier stage studies in metastases to the choroid and cancers of the ocular surface are ongoing. Aura's mission is to improve outcomes for patients living with ocular cancers by delivering a therapy that not only arrests tumor growth but also preserves vision and quality of life.

For more information, visit aurabiosciences.com. Follow us on X, @AuraBiosciences, and visit us on LinkedIn.

Position Summary

Aura Biosciences is seeking a highly motivated Clinical Scientist, Contractor to join our Clinical Development organization.

The Clinical Scientist will be a key scientific member of cross-functional study teams, contributing to the design, execution, analysis, interpretation, and communication of Aura's clinical programs. Working closely with the Vice President Clinical Development and colleagues across Medical, Clinical Operations, Biostatistics, Safety, Data Management, Regulatory, and other functions, this individual will help translate clinical strategy into high-quality studies and actionable scientific evidence.

The successful candidate will combine strong scientific and clinical judgment with a hands-on approach to clinical data, study execution, and cross-functional problem solving.

Key Responsibilities

Clinical Data Review and Study Execution

  • Conduct ongoing review and interpretation of clinical trial data, including safety, efficacy, study conduct, and data quality.
  • Identify emerging clinical trends, inconsistencies, and data issues and work cross-functionally and proactively to drive timely resolution.
  • Partner with Biostatistics and Data Management on data review plans, patient profiles, listings, tables, figures, data cleaning, and database lock activities.
  • Serve as a clinical-science resource for study teams and partner with Clinical Operations to support high-quality study execution.

Clinical Development and Regulatory

  • Contribute clinical and scientific input to clinical development plans, study design, and analysis approaches.
  • Author and/or contribute to protocols and amendments, clinical study reports, investigator brochures, regulatory briefing documents, health authority responses, and other key clinical documents.
  • Evaluate emerging clinical data, scientific literature, and competitive programs to inform study and development strategy.
  • Ensure clinical data and scientific rationale are presented clearly, accurately, and consistently across clinical and regulatory deliverables.

Scientific Communication

  • Develop clear presentations of clinical data for study teams, internal governance, and external scientific audiences.
  • Contribute to abstracts, posters, presentations, manuscripts, and other scientific communications.
  • Maintain current knowledge of ocular oncology, ophthalmology, oncology drug development, and the evolving therapeutic landscape relevant to Aura's programs.

Cross-Functional Collaboration

  • Collaborate effectively across Clinical Development, Clinical Operations, Biostatistics, Data Management, Safety, Regulatory Affairs, and other functions.
  • Communicate clinical insights, risks, and recommendations clearly and bring a patient-focused, evidence-based perspective to decision-making.
  • Help develop fit-for-purpose clinical-science processes and ways of working appropriate for a growing biotechnology company.
  • Demonstrate scientific rigor, accountability, flexibility, and a willingness to work across traditional functional boundaries.

Qualifications

  • Advanced degree in a relevant scientific or health-related discipline (PhD, PharmD, OD, or equivalent) strongly preferred; candidates with an MS, MPH, or other relevant advanced degree and substantial clinical development experience may also be considered.
  • 3+ years of relevant experience in clinical research or drug development within biotechnology, pharmaceuticals, or medical devices.
  • Experience supporting the conduct, analysis, and reporting of interventional clinical trials.
  • Demonstrated ability to review and interpret clinical and scientific data and translate findings into clear conclusions and recommendations.
  • Strong understanding of clinical trial methodology, GCP, and relevant regulatory requirements.
  • Strong scientific writing, presentation, communication, and cross-functional collaboration skills.
  • Ability to take ownership, manage multiple priorities, and deliver high-quality work in a fast-paced, evolving environment.

Preferred Experience

  • Experience in ophthalmology, oncology, or rare disease drug development.
  • Experience with Phase 2 and/or Phase 3 clinical development.
  • Hands-on experience with efficacy and safety data review, including patient profiles, listings, tables, and figures.
  • Experience contributing to regulatory submissions or interactions with health authorities is a plus.

Travel

Ability to travel domestically and internationally as required for study activities and other business needs. Expected travel approximately 10–20%.

Contract Expecations:

Remote role in UK (not limited to London posting location)

Must be physically located in UK

Full time weekly hours (40 hours per week)

Expectations for year-long contractor (possibility for both/either extention/conversion depending on business need)

Must be authorized to work legally in UK

jobs.excerpt: The Organization In the face of overwhelming legal and practical barriers, many migrants who have suffered exploitation or abuse at the hands of employers or government officials give up their rights after leaving the United States.
jobs.description:
The Organization

In the face of overwhelming legal and practical barriers, many migrants who have suffered exploitation or abuse at the hands of employers or government officials give up their rights after leaving the United States. Other migrants who flee abuse, violence, and persecution are unable to remain in safety due to lack of evidence to support their claims.

These migrants need “portable justice” – the right and ability to access justice across borders. Justice in Motion is dedicated to ensuring portable justice through legal, educational, and policy initiatives in the U.S., Mexico, and Central America. Essential to this transnational model is our Defender Network, a unique partnership of on-the-ground human rights organizations in Mexico and Central America. Justice in Motion makes sure that wherever migrants go, their rights will follow.

The Position

The Legal Manager will join the Legal Action team and ensure projects run smoothly and in alignment with Justice in Motion’s theory of social change and program work goals, with the guidance and under the supervision of the Legal Director. The Legal Manager will lead case collaborations and activities so that migrants have access to cross-border justice through international collaborations between advocates based in the U.S. and human rights defenders based in Mexico and Central America.

The ideal candidate is a lawyer who has represented immigrant clients in cases with cross-border elements and who is also an effective project manager. While the initial focus of this position will be related to migrants who are seeking protection in the U.S. or whose rights are violated in the U.S. during their arrest, detention and deportation, including parents who are deported without their children, over time the areas of concentration may shift as strategic opportunities arise. The candidate must possess professional fluency in Spanish and English (written and spoken), which will be assessed as the first step of our hiring process. As this job will require periodic in-person collaboration building to advance portable justice, the candidate must be willing and able to travel internationally.

Note: Justice in Motion does not represent clients directly; this position does not include direct legal services.

Ideal Candidate Profile

Strong candidates for this role will bring the following to this position:

  1. 5+ years of immigration legal experience representing clients from Mexico and Central America in humanitarian immigration matters.
    Candidates must hold a JD or LLM from an accredited U.S. law school and experience practicing law in the United States. Experience with federal civil litigation advancing civil rights claims on behalf of migrant clients is a plus. This is someone who has appreciated their time practicing law but is eager to work on tackling systemic issues related to access to justice on a project-level.
  2. Professional English / Spanish Fluency: This role requires bilingual fluency in spoken and written English and Spanish, including legal analysis, client communication, document review, and professional collaboration across languages. This is someone who can easily switch back and forth and pick up nuances accurately, with comprehension consistently nearing 100%. Learn more about this requirement under the “Required Professional Language Fluency” section of this job description.
  3. Strong project management skills: Experience managing multiple workstreams simultaneously, maintaining detailed project plans, and tracking deadlines. This is someone who has led initiatives from start to finish.
  4. Tech-savvy: Proficiency with Excel and Word, Google Workspace, Adobe Acrobat, project management tools such as Asana. Experience with Salesforce or comparable case management systems is a plus. This is someone who easily picks up and adapts to new technologies and systems.
  5. A collaborative partner: Demonstrates emotional intelligence, self-awareness, and patience. Able to work effectively with colleagues and stakeholders with diverse cultural backgrounds who may have different visions for how social change happens.
  6. An effective communicator: Skilled at clarifying what’s being requested, checking for understanding, communicating progress, and surfacing potential issues before they become major problems.
  7. Adaptability: Comfortable navigating changing priorities, balancing creative planning while adjusting to meet changing circumstances.
  8. Cross-cultural awareness: Experience living and/or working in multicultural environments and a demonstrated ability to engage diverse communities with curiosity, empathy, and respect.
  9. Connected to our mission: Experience with or passion for migrant rights, access to justice, and cross-border advocacy is strongly preferred. Familiarity with the challenges facing migrant communities from Mexico and Central America is a necessity.

Responsibilities

The primary responsibility includes project management supporting Justice in Motion’s collaborative casework to ensure portable justice for migrants. This is an important position on a small team, and duties may evolve over time based on strategic opportunity and the team capacity. The primary areas of responsibility include:

Case Collaboration Management (40%):

  • Manage cross-border case collaborations involving advocates in the U.S. and members of Justice in Motion’s Defender Network in Mexico and Central America.
  • Conduct intake conversations with advocates and assess cases identified for potential Defender Network collaboration.
  • Provide guidance to advocates and Defenders on portable justice issues and help troubleshoot communication or coordination challenges.
  • Track case-collaborations through regular follow-up, check-ins, and evaluation.
  • Coordinate administrative aspects of case collaboration, including payments, invoices, documentation, and outcome tracking.
  • Prepare narrative summaries and reports documenting case progress, outcomes, and lessons learned.

Project Management (20%):

  • Manage special projects that advance Justice in Motion’s portable justice and access-to-justice strategies.
  • Develop and maintain project plans, workflows, timelines, and tracking systems to support effective implementation.
  • Coordinate program implementation, administration, data collection, outcome reporting, and other project-related activities.
  • Facilitate meetings, convenings, and other collaborative activities involving internal and external stakeholders.
  • Identify and address project barriers, emerging needs, and opportunities for improvement.

Relationship Management and Cross-Border Collaboration (15%)

  • Build and maintain strong working relationships with members of the Justice in Motion Defender Network in Mexico and Central America.
  • Develop collaborative working relationships with advocates and organizations in the U.S. who represent migrants who may benefit from Defender Network assistance.
  • Serve as a consistent point of coordination across partners, helping ensure clear communication, shared expectations, and effective collaboration.
  • Navigate cross-cultural and cross-organizational relationships with professionalism, empathy, and cultural awareness.

Legal Expertise, Analysis, and Advisory Support (15%):

  • Maintain strong substantive knowledge of immigration law and procedure, cross-border legal issues, and US migration and labor policies affecting migrants from Mexico and Central America.
  • Provide legal analysis and guidance related to immigration enforcement, humanitarian relief, migrant rights, and portable justice.
  • Identify emerging legal or policy developments that may affect Justice in Motion’s case collaboration work or the communities served through the Defender Network.
  • Share relevant legal knowledge and developments with colleagues and partners as appropriate.

Legal Training and Writing (10%):

  • Develop and deliver training (virtual and in-person) in Spanish and English for advocates, Defenders, and other constituencies.
  • Draft legal practice resources, advisories, and other materials in English and Spanish related to migrants rights, immigration, and access to justice.
  • Translate complex legal and policy concepts into practical, accessible information for varied audiences.
  • Contribute to the development of tools and resources that strengthen the capacity of advocates and Defender Network members.

Required Professional Language Proficiency: This role requires professional fluency in both English and Spanish. A successful candidate can:

  • Conduct complex professional and legal conversations in both English and Spanish, including the ability to communicate key information across languages in real time.
  • Produce high quality written materials in English and Spanish without reliance on external translation tools or resources.
  • Accurately interpret nuanced, technical, and sensitive information in real time.
  • Adapt tone, terminology, and cultural context appropriately for diverse audiences.

Details: This is a full-time, exempt position that reports to the Legal Director. This is a union position and will be covered by Justice in Motion’s collective bargaining agreement. Union employees are represented by the Association of Legal Aid Attorneys, UAW Local 2325.

Location and Travel: Justice in Motion is a U.S.-based, remote organization. This position is remote and based in the United States but may require occasional domestic and international travel. The position will operate on Eastern Time Zone hours. This position will require occasional travel to Central America, Mexico and within the U.S.

Salary and Benefits: Salary is based on the scale in the collective bargaining agreement, with a starting range for this position of $76,000 (Step 6) to $84,750 (Step 11), depending on experience. Justice in Motion provides a very competitive benefits package, including: 100% employer-paid healthcare for individual employees plus partial family coverage; 3% 401k annual contribution, work-from-home and home office setup stipends; our office is closed 12/24-1/1 plus other paid holidays. Additional PTO includes 12 days paid vacation in the first year, 12 sick days, and 5 personal days. A fully paid sabbatical is offered after 7 years of service.

HOW TO APPLY:

Justice in Motion is an equal opportunity employer, and all persons are encouraged to apply. Applications will be accepted through our hiring portal.

Justice in Motion is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of race, ethnicity, national origin, religion, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, disability, age, marital status, or any other applicable status protected by state or local law.

Salary: $76,000 to $84,750

You'll build and run the systems behind our partner program, including HubSpot workflows and email sequences, partner tiers and health scores, deal registration, and partner content. About VIDIZMO

VIDIZMO is an AI software company, founded in 2009 and headquartered in Tysons, Virginia. Our products are Nexus, AI Intelligence Hub, AI Live Insight, and Redactor. Together they help organizations store, search, analyze, redact, and share unstructured data, and they treat video, audio, images, documents, and text as equally important sources.

More than 100 organizations use VIDIZMO in production across public safety and justice, government, healthcare, financial services, education, legal, manufacturing, and energy. Many run it on-premises, in air-gapped setups, or in FedRAMP High environments, on an architecture aligned with the CJIS Security Policy.

As an independent software vendor, we sell directly and through a global network of channel partners who sell, deploy, and service VIDIZMO for their own clients. Partners are central to how we grow, and this role builds the systems that keep that network running smoothly. VIDIZMO is an NVIDIA Inception partner, a Microsoft Solutions Partner for Data & AI, and ISO/IEC 27001:2022 certified. Customers can buy through GSA, Carahsoft, and state and cooperative contract vehicles.

AI tools like Claude, ChatGPT and Copilot are part of how we work, and we expect you to use them well. Ownership is not negotiable: you check anything AI helps produce for accuracy, completeness and compliance, and you're accountable for the final result.

What You'll Do

  • Build and run the partner program in HubSpot, including workflows, email sequences, partner tiers and health scores.
  • Own the deal registration form and the partner dashboard and keep both accurate and working.
  • Make sure every partner deal registration reaches business development within one working day.
  • Publish partner content, including partner emails, enablement materials and the partner pages on our website.

  • Legally authorized to work in Pakistan.

What Sets You Apart

You think like an engineer. When something breaks, you fix it, and when something works, you measure it so you can do more of it. You build systems that run reliably without constant attention, you use AI tools to work faster and automate the routine, and you take ownership of the partner program's operations with little supervision.

How You're Paid

This role includes a monthly salary plus performance-based commission.

Health insurance (OPD/IPD), separate maternity coverage, leave encashment, referral bonus, EOBI, yearly increments, provident fund, bonus, and clear career growth.

You will own the operational foundation that makes every marketing dollar accountable—driving consistency in tracking, reporting, and governance while enabling the team to scale. A key part of this role is unifying data across disparate systems into a trusted, single view of marketing performance, ensuring accuracy and availability for decision-making

Testing & Incrementality
